Five seasons of “Hacks.” Five Emmy Awards for Jean Smart.

Smart completed an undefeated run Monday night, winning lead actress in a comedy series for every season of the acclaimed HBO Max comedy and becoming the first woman to win an acting Emmy for every season of a television series.

The audience rose for a standing ovation as Smart, 75, made her way to the stage for her fifth victory as legendary Las Vegas comedian Deborah Vance. Smart immediately turned the moment into material.

“Just the men stay standing. The girls get to sit down,” she joked.

It’s her eighth trophy overall, which ties the all-time performer record shared by Cloris Leachman and Julia Louis-Dreyfus. Smart also becomes the first to win best actress for each season of a show’s run.

Smart, who first got noticed in the CBS comedy “Designing Women,” won her first Emmys for guest appearances on “Frasier” and then another for a supporting role on “Samantha Who.”

The victory gave Smart her fifth lead comedy actress Emmy for “Hacks,” which debuted in 2021 and ended its five-season run in May.

Smart dedicated the award to the creative team behind the series: Lucia Aniello, Jen Statsky and Paul W. Downs.

“It all begins and ends with them,” Smart said. “I love you guys so much.”

She also thanked HBO, Universal, her representatives and her children, Forrest and Connor, whom she called her “anchor.”

Then, with the clock counting down on both her speech and a remarkable five-season run, Smart summed it up simply: “What a ride!”

She punctuated the moment by tossing her Emmy into the air and catching it before leaving the stage.

Julia Louis-Dreyfus came close to accomplishing the same feat with “Veep,” winning lead comedy actress six consecutive times. But Louis-Dreyfus lost for the show’s seventh and final season to “Fleabag” star Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

Smart had played down the significance of the potential record before Monday’s ceremony. During an August appearance on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” she called the distinction a “technicality” and pointed to Louis-Dreyfus’ larger collection of Emmy victories.

“I’ve got to give it to Julia Louis-Dreyfus,” Smart said.

Her three Emmys outside “Hacks” came for two guest appearances on “Frasier” and a supporting comedy actress victory for “Samantha Who?” Smart has received 15 Emmy nominations during her career.

“Hacks” follows the unlikely partnership between Vance and Ava Daniels, the younger comedy writer played by Hannah Einbinder. The series became an Emmy fixture during its run, with previous victories including outstanding comedy series and supporting comedy actress for Einbinder.

Since “Hacks” premiered, the only performer other than Smart to win lead comedy actress was Quinta Brunson for “Abbott Elementary” at the January 2024 ceremony, when “Hacks” did not have a new season in contention.

For her final turn as Deborah Vance, Smart prevailed over a field that included Elle Fanning for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” and Lisa Kudrow for “The Comeback.”

News.title: Newcastle rocked and Elland Road rocking after Leeds complete demolition job
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Tech stocks have fallen sharply after Elon Musk and the boss of OpenAI joined calls for the slowdown of AI development. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Hundreds of hotels, pubs and restaurants urge Burnham to slash VAT | Prime Minister challenged to honour pledge to cut levy to 10pc and save thousands of jobs

2) Trump rejects Silicon Valley’s calls for AI slowdown | US president says ‘very negative forces’ are overstating the risks

3) Labour’s wealth raid ‘kills off ultra-luxury homes in London’ | A 120-home project in St John’s Wood is likely to be the last residence of its kind

4) Factories slash hiring ahead of Budget | Manufacturing vacancies fall by 6.2pc, despite rising business confidence

5) David Lloyd waters down net zero targets | Gym chain has spent millions on solar panels and heat pumps in effort to cut emissions

What happened overnight

Asian stocks fell as traders assessed fresh safety concerns over the pace of AI development.

South Korea’s Kospi lost 3.3pc to 6,679.23 and Japan’s Nikkei 225 index slid 0.6pc to 63,633.57. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 24,886.81.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq index dropped 1.2pc in Asian trading hours, while S&P 500 futures shed 0.5pc. Those linked to The Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.1pc.

It came despite efforts from Donald Trump to downplay concerns about AI technology, saying on Sunday that “very negative forces” were overstating the risks.

On Saturday, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for tech companies to slow down their advancement and for more work to be done on AI safety. His comments were backed by Sam Altman, the OpenAI boss, Sir Demis Hassabis, the chairman of Google DeepMind, and Elon Musk.

Oil rose after Saudi Arabia was forced to close a crucial oil pipeline after drone attacks from Iraq on Friday. Brent crude was up 2.8pc to $107.5 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate rose 2.22pc to $102.3 a barrel.

The US’s 10-year Treasury yields edged closer to the crucial 5pc level on Friday amid the prolonged bond sell-off, while two-year yields climbed to 4.66pc.

News.title: Asia on high alert as El Niño threatens new Dengue epidemic
News.content:
Countries from Brazil to Taiwan are bracing for a surge in dengue driven by the “supersized” El Niño, as the UN warns this year’s weather phenomenon could be the strongest on record.

Both the virus and the Aedes mosquitoes that transmit it are especially sensitive to heat – and the El Niño is expected to push global temperatures to new highs.

“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary General, said last week. “The ​science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.”

The weather phenomenon – a periodic warming of sea surface temperature in the eastern Pacific, caused by weakening trade winds – alters rainfall and temperature patterns across the globe. That, in turn, causes extreme weather like droughts, heatwaves, floods and typhoons – which then trigger events including wildfires, crop failures and a collapse in affected fisheries.

But it can also have a major impact on the transmission of disease, including dengue – and countries across the world, especially in Asia and Latin America, are bracing for outbreaks.

In July, Brazil’s Ministry of Health sent an alert warning states that arboviruses like dengue, chikungunya and Zika could surge later this year, and urged officials to ramp up disease surveillance and mosquito control programmes.

The increase will likely peak in 2027: the biomedical research institute Fiocruz has estimated that Brazil will see 1.7 million dengue cases next year, driven by El Niño.

News.title: ‘Your home is your palace’: Queen Elizabeth II’s housekeeper answers reader questions
News.content:
Was there one surprisingly simple trick used in the palace that made things feel instantly more polished?

Jay, West Midlands

Making sure you have a routine is the best way for everything to feel polished. At the palace, the team is trained, and everyone has the right tools and time to do their job... They learned how to lift things safely and how to be confident when they were around the Royal Collection. When you’re cleaning historic areas such as palaces and castles, you have to make sure you don’t overdo it. We had a daily routine that ensured we didn’t over-clean everything.

What is the royal protocol for dealing with ironing and maintaining perfectly crisp sheets without using harsh, eco-unfriendly chemicals?

Saleem, London

Much of what would be classed as royal protocol are things we would do in our own homes. For linen, you need to treat it well and look after it by not washing it at too high a temperature or using too much detergent. Make sure the products you’re using are eco-friendly, not only for the environment, but also to care for the linen. For historic linen, it needs to be handled very gently, as it can tear quite easily.

Did the Queen get involved in any of the details of housekeeping?

Peter, East of England

I was very blessed. The Queen did leave it up to me to make those decisions because she trusted me to keep her home and the other royal residences clean and up to a great standard. I kept in touch with her, making sure the team was involved. We would have regular update meetings to ensure everyone knew what was happening and when. There was planned cleaning throughout the year depending on what was occurring, making sure certain areas were protected or closed off, for example.

I would feel very stressed cleaning around objects of great value, history and sentiment. How do you avoid disasters?

Catherine, North West

It’s important the team feels confident when cleaning those areas. We achieve that through training and building their confidence.

In the castle, we introduced a cleaning schedule that covered different areas within the state apartments – and it meant that we didn’t over-clean. The structure of this schedule was important. Every day, we would ensure we vacuumed and damp-dusted; there were no actual chemicals or any what I call “wet chemicals”. On a Monday, for instance, we would clean vases. On a Tuesday, we would do the fireplaces. On a Wednesday, it would be light fittings.

It’s crucial the team is given the right amount of time to clean, so that they don’t feel rushed or stressed. But we also have to remember that accidents happen. And if an accident happens and it was just an accident, then what can you do? It’s just one of those things.

Ultimately, making sure people are trained and confident is the key.

With limited time, what are the housekeeping priorities?

David, South West

My housekeeping priorities when at home are to make things look really tidy quickly. Putting your newspapers away, fluffing the cushions up, tidying the curtains, making sure your washing is cleared and the dishwasher is on – these are all things that will make a big difference, even if you haven’t had time to get your mop or vacuum out.

When are you satisfied a room is clean?

D, North West

I am quite a hard taskmaster and I do like perfection, but equally, that comes with making sure people understand the guidelines and what’s expected of them, after being trained properly.

I like to be visible and around the team, showing them what I’m looking at. I would get them to sit on a toilet and then shut the door, so they could see what’s behind the door – or sit in the bath, because that way you can see what other people are seeing when they’re using it. If you’re cleaning and rushing around, you don’t always see those little details.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends warning to Max Dowman, 16, after wonderkid was left out of Arsenal squad and dropped down to U21s
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA has warned Max Dowman he must “earn” his minutes like “anybody else” after leaving the wonderkid out of his matchday squad.

Dowman, 16, was left out of Arteta’s squad to face Sunderland at the weekend and instead played the full 90 minutes for the Gunners’ Under-21s against Chelsea.



It was the second time that Dowman has been part of the U21 side this season, despite a breakout campaign last term.

The teenager is yet to get any senior minutes this season and although Arteta has promised those chances will come, he reiterated that Dowman must work hard to earn them.



The Arsenal boss said: “I wish we could have him [against Sunderland], but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have.

“He will have his chance, he will have his minutes, and he will have to earn them like anybody else.

“We know the talent that we have, we know the player that we have there, and we need to help him and find a way to make sure that he continues to develop and help the team.”

Dowman became the Premier League’s youngest ever player and youngest ever goalscorer last season as he burst onto the scene in North London.

And the record-breaker could be given the nod for the first time this term when Arsenal take on Ipswich Town in the League Cup third round on Tuesday.

Arteta knows that he has to rotate his squad this season if he wants to go deep in all competitions, having suffered defeat to Manchester City in last season’s League Cup final.

Sports.title: Leeds 4 Newcastle 1: Calvert-Lewin stakes England claim as Daniel Farke’s men run riot to hammer Toon
Sports.content:
RED-HOT Leeds smashed Matthias Jaissle’s unbeaten Newcastle record to pieces with an electrifying first-half display.

The Mags were waving the white flag by the break after Lewis Miley’s own-goal before Jayden Bogle and Dominic Calvert-Lewin blew them away.



And Jaissle’s former Red Bull Salzburg star Noah Okafor rubbed more salt in the wounds in the second half to round-off the 4-1 thumping.

German Jaissle’s honeymoon is well and truly over, but compatriot Daniel Farke has Whites fans dreaming of Europe as they climbed into third.



Four matches undefeated. A captain in Ethan Ampadu who continues to grow into a midfield monster. And, most importantly, an England striker in Calvert-Lewin who cannot stop scoring.

Despite the huge summer of change at Newcastle, some things remain the same. And Jaissle will be just as sick of the sight of him as the Toon Army.

This was Calvert-Lewin’s eighth career goal against the Magpies – his most against any opponent.

He and Leeds were just too hot to handle for the shellshocked Toon, who appeared to be flying under the new man. But the numbers have told a different story.



His side have been playing with fire all this season and they finally got burned in West Yorkshire.

Newcastle had conceded a worrying 61 shots in their opening three Prem games. Fortunately, £25.7million summer signing Lukas Hornicek got to work fast, making 13 saves across those matches.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But despite several more spectacular ones here, the Czech keeper was powerless to stop the Leeds storm.

The bright lights of Elland Road were always going to be Jaissle’s toughest test yet. Leeds have been formidable here since Farke’s arrival in 2023, suffering just one defeat now in 26 evening league kick offs.

That has earned the nickname “Farke After Dark” amongst Leeds supporters. And on this form, it could be European nights soon.



Jaissle, who confirmed in-form winger Anthony Elanga could be out long-term before kick-off with an unspecified injury, also lost £48m midfielder Nico Gonzalez to a head injury midway through the half.

But their downfall had already begun. Their £51m forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo was lucky to avoid a nightmare debut when he went unpunished for palming the ball away in his own box with less than a minute on the clock.

Hornicek saved his side with a brilliant scoop away from Jayden Bogle’s close-range spin and turn before tipping over the wing-back’s volley.



But Ao Tanaka’s strike first hit Sean Steur – on for Gonzalez – and then Lewis Miley, wrong-footing Hornicek as he stood powerless and watched the ball hit the net.

Moments later it was two and another nightmare for Steur. His underhit pass was pounced on by Bogle.

Within a flash it was worked wide and Calvert-Lewin and Bogle both rose about Sven Botman, the former’s header hitting the latter and going in.

The floodgates were open and Leeds smelt blood. Hornicek’s double save prevented Ampadu and DCL but there was no stopping the hotshot on the stroke of half time.

He sent Botman to the papershop when dragging it back on his right foot before pulling the trigger, the shot taking a slight knick off Malick Thiaw on its way in.



This was the first time Leeds had scored three in the first half of a Premier League game at home since May 2001.



That day they got five against Bradford and they quickly set about adding to their tally following the restart.

It was four with half an hour to go when Newcastle failed to clear a long throw. It dropped for Okafor, and he lashed home a half-volley past the diving Hornicek.

That was the icing on the cake for the Whites and Farke.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Toon legend Alan Shearer labelled it a “s*** show”. Sub Bazoumana Toure grabbed a consolation at the death but this was a rude awakening for Jaissle and the Mags.

But for Leeds, this could be the start of something special.

Sports.title: West Ham legend Billy Bonds leaves staggering sum to his daughters after death aged 79
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL great Billy Bonds left his daughters more than £575,000 in his will, documents show.

The star played 799 times for West Ham, captaining them to 1975 and 1980 FA Cup wins.



He went on to manage the club, had a stand named after him at the London Stadium and was made an MBE in 1988.

Bonds’ will was written in June 2023, three years after his wife of 52 years, Marilyn, died.



He died aged 79 in November last year at a care home in Chislehurst, Kent.

The value of his estate after deductions was £575,068, which daughters Claire and Katie share.

When he died, they said: “We are heartbroken to announce that we lost our beloved Dad.

“He was devoted to his family and was the most kind, loyal, selfless, and loving person.

“Dad loved West Ham United and its wonderful supporters with all his heart and treasured every moment of his time at the Club.

“He will always be in our hearts and eternally missed. We take comfort knowing that his legacy will live on forever.”



It comes as it was confirmed today that ex-West Ham goalie Ludek Miklosko – who played under Bonds in the Premier League when was manager – died.

The 64-year-old lost a battle with cancer.

Sports.title: Tactics Exposed: Why Man Utd must change ‘vacuum transition’ tactic as pressure builds on Carrick after derby nightmare
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED were humbled by ten-man Manchester City because Michael Carrick failed to adapt, while Enzo Maresca did.

Erling Haaland‘s controversial strike proved to be the difference between the two sides as City left Old Trafford with three points following a superb defensive display.



While much of the talk in the aftermath has been over the error made by VAR for Enzo Fernandez’s offside in the build up to the winner, this game showed the Red Devils paid the price for failing to shift tactics.

In the latest episode of SunSport’s award-winning series, Tactics Exposed, Dean Scoggins breaks down why Man Utd were unable to beat their rivals even after they went down to 10-men after Phil Foden was sent off.



Dean explains that Carrick set up his team for a transition game where they would have less of the ball and hit City on the break.

However, after Foden’s dismissal for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, Maresca made appropriate changes by subbing on Iliman Ndiaye for Rayan Cherki.



Meanwhile, Carrick failed to adapt his strategy, with his team paying the price for having a “vacuum” up front.

Dean explains that City bringing on Ndiaye emphasized their ball-carriers as a defensive outlet — which we are dubbing Maresca’s “carrier pigeon tactic”.

And despite only coming on halfway through the game, Ndiaye had 10 ball carries, which he took 147 metres, and six dribbles.

Likewise, Antoine Semenyo, Mateus Nunes, Elliot Anderson and Haaland also had more than 150 metres of ball carrying each.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Anderson was particularly impressive in covering spaces in front of the City backline, while also making a huge impact up the field.

He was even in the United box when Josko Gvardiol crossed the ball for Haaland’s far-post tap-in.

But the City defence was helped massively by United having no presence up front.

Carrick set them up to have a “transitional vacuum” that split Mateus Cunha and Fernandes as two false nines.

It looked like working in the opening stages when the game was 11v11.



However, when Foden was dismissed by Michael Oliver, Carrick needed to add some muscle up front to try to break down the City defence.



Carrick failed to do this until the 66th minute when City were already ahead.

Benjamin Sesko‘s introduction gave them some much-needed presence in the area, but the poor quality of Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu in wide areas limited their scoring opportunities.

Carrick realised all-too late that he needed Sesko as a foil to play through the middle to bring other attackers into the game.

Ultimately, United have work to do to fix their flawed attack, or else they face another disastrous season.

Sports.title: Howard Webb set to give public explanation in next 24 hours for astonishing VAR blunder over Haaland goal at Man Utd

REFS’ chief Howard Webb is set to explain tonight how the staggering Old Trafford VAR blunder unfolded.

Video ref Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus paid the price for their howler with both dropped from duties.

Webb will be able to play out the communication between Donohue and Antrobus in the Stockley Park video booth before Michael Oliver was told to signal the goal for City.

Webb gave the green light for Pro Ref to make a public admission of the “error of judgement” within three hours of the final whistle on Sunday.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star tipped for stardom by Wenger waited 12 YEARS for first Premier League goal – now he can shock Gunners
Sports.content:
CHUBA AKPOM was once tipped to be Arsenal’s main man, now he is in line to play against the Gunners after a rollercoaster journey.

Akpom, now 30, could feature against Arsenal on Tuesday when Ipswich host Mikel Arteta’s side in the League Cup third round.



The experienced striker has taken the scenic route to return to the Premier League with Ipswich this season.

His goal against Manchester United last month was his first in the Prem, coming 12 years and 350 days after Arsene Wenger handed him his debut for Arsenal as a 17-year-old.



That remarkable wait means he has the third-longest gap between debut and first goal in Prem history, behind only Damien Delany and Jack Robinson.

And it is the perfect illustration of Akpom’s unconventional career to date, a journey that has seen him play across 12 different teams in five different countries.



Akpom was always amongst the highest-rated youngsters in Arsenal’s academy, earning a stellar reputation when he was picked up aged just six from Rippleway FC after scoring over 100 goals in just two seasons.

Former Arsenal Under-21 boss and Head of Academy Coaching Terry Burton remembers expectations always being high for Akpom, from both the staff and the fans.

He told SunSport: “I think he always had that when he was coming through the academy.

“There were always people talking about Chuba, he was always held up to be a potential star player.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Sometimes at a younger age you don’t realise that it’s not enough to have people saying it, you have got to actually do it and achieve it.”

Akpom was a regular fixture of the England youth setup too, given his enormous potential, and Under-19s boss Noel Blake reckons his qualities are the same today as they were back then.

Blake told SunSport: “What you see with Chuba now, you saw it then. His shape hasn’t changed, his physicality and his stature.

“But his feet were frightening. He had excellent feet. He could play as a striker as a No10 and in the pockets.”



But despite such incredible promise, Akpom never managed to break into the Arsenal first team.

He left in 2018 after making just 12 appearances and spending most of his time on loan at Brentford, Coventry, Nottingham Forest, Hull, Brighton and Belgian side Sint-Truiden.

You would be forgiven for thinking a move to the lower leagues was on the cards, but Akpom opted for a rarely-trodden path – joining Greek top-flight side PAOK.

Aged 22 at the time, Akpom helped PAOK to an unbeaten league campaign with six goals – including a crucial winner against title rivals Olympiacos.



And he topped it off with an overhead kick to win the Greek Cup final and turn an invincible season into a double.

Akpom’s former PAOK team-mate, Omar El Kaddouri, told SunSport: “It was the perfect step for him. We were playing in Europe so he could show himself to the whole of Europe.

“Not a lot of people knew of him outside of England and I think PAOK was the perfect step for him. He got better, he improved a lot.”

Akpom would watch Arsenal games on the team bus and support his former club from a distance in Greece, keeping a special place in his heart for the team that first gave him a chance.



But when the opportunity to return to England came, it was Middlesbrough who came knocking.

The striker joined Boro in 2020, and after two seasons of struggle in the Championship, Akpom was on the brink of leaving the club after being made to train with the U21s by boss Chris Wilder.

That all changed when Michael Carrick came in to replace Wilder and Akpom thrived, winning the Championship Golden Boot with 28 goals in 38 games.

A £12m move to Ajax followed, where Akpom spent two seasons and scored 23 goals before securing another European adventure in a switch to French club Lille on loan.

But it was last season when the lure of England crept back in and Akpom joined Ipswich on loan with a view to making the deal permanent this summer.



Now, after his remarkable journey, he finds himself facing the club where it all started.

Former England youth boss Blake said: “Ask any England coach at that time, they will tell you Chuba always had a terrific attitude.

“He was determined. He has great strength of character, a great resilience and he was determined to achieve something in the game.



“Whatever that may look like. He definitely had ability, resilience and a willingness to win.”

That willingness to win may have seen him regularly fighting team-mates in training while in Greece, but it is also the reason he is now taking on Arsenal back in England.

El Kaddouri added: “It is going to be emotional for him. It is his team. When he was playing for PAOK he used to follow them, watch their games and cheer for them.

“It is a special club for him and it is always special to play the team where you grew up. I am sure he will still be trying to score.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I have played with some of the best players in the world, like Gonzalo Higuain, Marek Hamsik and Edinson Cavani.



“The biggest difference between them and others is being competitive and wanting to win even in training and being competitive all the time. Chuba has that.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta compared to Sir Alex Ferguson after Arsenal take drastic referee action
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta compared to Sir Alex Ferguson after Arsenal take drastic referee action

Arsenal secured their fourth win from as many Premier League games against Sunderland but Mikel Arteta was left furious with a refereeing decision after the game

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta was fuming after Sunderland were awarded a controversial penalty against Sunderland (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher has branded Mikel Arteta 'the Sir Alex Ferguson' of the modern Premier League era after the Arsenal boss described the penalty given against his side as 'not acceptable'. The Gunners might have maintained their perfect start to the season with a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland on Saturday night, but the Spaniard was left furious by the penalty decision that went against his team.

‌



A dramatic second-half saw referee John Brooks point to the spot when Dan Ballard was brought down by Ezri Konsa, and David Raya parried Enzo Le Fee’s subsequent effort onto the left post. But that didn’t stop Arteta from fuming about the decision in his post-match press conference.

‌



Former United boss Ferguson would always make his feelings known on decisions that went against his side during his time in charge at Old Trafford, and Carragher, speaking on Monday Night Football, believes Arteta came across in the same way as the Scot once did. He said: “This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now.

‌



“He’s the 'Don' at the moment and the Premier League champion. There are a lot of new managers about, he’s been in his role for six or seven years and he feels he is in a position of power to say it wasn’t a penalty and I don’t think it was a penalty.

“But it will be interesting to see how long it takes for another referee to give a penalty against Arsenal in a similar situation.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“But I thought it was very interesting in the press conference, one of the journalists made a point about no matter what question you asked him he kept going back to the penalty.

“He was determined to get the narrative out that this won’t happen again to his club, but listen that is management. We have seen it with Alex Ferguson, with Jose Mourinho.”

‌



Agreeing with Carragher, former Luton Town and Wolves boss Rob Edwards said: “I think Jamie is right, he is putting himself in a position where he is looking after his team and football club and people will listen to a Premier League winning manager. They will listen as he is a powerful voice there.”

On the penalty decision, Edwards said: “We don’t want to see the crappling or the pulling for long periods, but I don’t think it is (a penalty), Dave (Jones), I’m sorry.

View 3 Images Arsenal were furious after conceding a penalty during their win over Sunderland

‌



“You can see the grab from the angle we are going to get in a second but, I think Dan Ballard knows what he is doing and he pulls Konsa with him. I don’t think it is a penalty.”

Mirror Football reported on Monday that Arsenal have made contact with Howard Webb, Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer, as they want an explanation about why the decision was given by Brooks. And w hen asked for his thoughts on the decision on Saturday night, Arteta fumed: “The first question and we have to discuss this.

"This is not acceptable at this level because it was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium (that) was unbelievable. Sunderland they are so organised, so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues.

‌



View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson was known for his forthright views on refereeing decisions (Image: John Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

“We had to cope with all of that because it was a lot and a really difficult win after Chelsea and Napoli. On top of that we have to go through what we’ve done today that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

“I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they’d think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. I don’t know what to think really. I’m sad we have to discuss before the game something at this level that has the gravity of that.

Article continues below

“That changes the course of the season and it can cost you the Champions League. At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen.”

Sports.title: Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves
Sports.content:
Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves

Gary Neville believes there is one clear favourite for the Premier League crown this season with Arsenal and Manchester City both sat on 12 points after four games

View 2 Images Gary Neville has picked between Arsenal and Man City for the Premier League (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville feels Manchester City can now run Arsenal close in the title race after a flurry of late transfer activity - but they are not quite on the level of defending champions.

‌



Mikel Arteta oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title win for 22 years last term after finally besting Manchester City in the title race. Both sides have strengthened over the summer, although City are now under new management after Pep Guardiola decided to bring the curtain down on his trophy-laden reign in Manchester back in May.

‌



After two years away from their throne, City have reshaped their squad with big-money deals for Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi in the summer transfer window.

‌



But City have been told that Arsenal are still a better team, even though Neville feels they have closed the gap on their title rivals somewhat.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There was a point probably two or three weeks before the end of the transfer window when City didn’t have in Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez and Ndiaye that you thought they look well short, particularly in midfield," Neville told Sky Sports.

"They get those three in late on which is £250million worth of business I think and it’s transformed the look of the team."

City, like Arsenal, have a 100 per cent record in the Premier League from their opening four games after beating Manchester United in the Manchester derby on Sunday. Neville feels the availability of their experienced defenders will be crucial to any hopes City have of matching Arsenal stride for stride as the season progresses.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City have won all four of their Premier League games so far under Enzo Maresca (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

He added: "And I think the big thing for City is it’s going to come down to the defence. It’s going to come down to Dias being fit. It’s going to come down to Gvardiol being fit.

"The experienced players back there and Guehi, obviously. If you can keep that back four and you’ve got Khusanov on the bench and Nico O’Reilly, it’s a youngish back four as with some younger defenders.

‌



"If they don’t pick up injuries Manchester City they can give Arsenal a real run. I still think Arsenal are better, but City have improved enormously with the signings they made at the end of the window.

"That [beating Manchester United] was big for Maresca, to establish a big-game mentality."

Sports.title: Harry Maguire called VAR who allowed Erling Haaland goal a 'f****** joke'
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire called VAR who allowed Erling Haaland goal a 'f****** joke'

Manchester United were left feeling hard done by after a controversial VAR call at the weekend and one of the officials involved was in Harry Maguire's bad books earlier this year

View 3 Images Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby was given by VAR (Image: Getty)

Manchester United were left furious this weekend when VAR intervened to allow an offside goal scored by Erling Haaland to stand, costing them victory in the Manchester derby.

‌



Matt Donohue, the VAR official from the game, and his assistant have since been stood down from duty this weekend by Pro Ref, who issued an apology to United after Enzo Fernandez was ruled to have not played the ball despite attempting to reach Josko Gvardiol's cross while in an offside position.

‌



As the fallout from Sunday's derby continues, a previous outburst from Harry Maguire directed at Donohue has resurfaced.

‌



Back in March, he and his colleagues were branded a "f****** joke" by the central defender while operating as fourth official in Manchester United's 2-2 draw away at Bournemouth.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Maguire was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity on the south coast. Bournemouth were awarded a penalty for the offence with Maguire deemed to have pulled down Evanilson inside the penalty area.

That outburst earned Maguire an additional one match ban after Donohue shared the offensive remarks with an independent regulatory commission, claiming that Maguire said them as he left the field.

View 3 Images Harry Maguire was furious at the match officials, including Matt Donohue, after being sent off vs Bournemouth back in March (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Haaland's goal was originally ruled offside, only for VAR to intervene and overturn the decision. It quickly sparked a huge debate online with numerous pundits, including Gary Neville and Wayne Rooney, suggesting the VAR officials had got the call wrong.

An apology was issued just hours after the game, which Manchester City won 1-0. It read: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

‌



View 3 Images Donahue has been stood down from duty this weekend (Image: Alex Dodd/CameraSport)

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Sports.title: Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit
Sports.content:
Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal ace Robin van Persie is now embarking on a new project after his first senior managerial role came to an end

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has recently started a new role (Image: 2026 BSR Agency)

Former Manchester United and Arsenal forward Robin van Persie has become a global ambassador for e-bike brand ENGWE. At the end of last season, Van Persie's managerial role with Feyenoord came to an end after 16 months.

He earned Champions League qualification with the Dutch side after finishing second in the Eredivisie but was surprisingly relieved of his duties. The ex-striker's exit took place not long after the club appointed Devy Rigaux as technical director and Robert Eenhoorn as general manager.

Now, a few months after his departure, it's been announced that the Dutchman, who scored 144 goals and contributed 59 assists in 280 Premier League appearances, will work in an ambassadorial capacity for the global e-bike brand.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

After the new role with ENGWE was announced, Van Persie said: "Throughout my career, reliability has always mattered. Being able to trust the people around you, your equipment and your decisions.

"That is one of the things that attracted me to ENGWE. Today, staying active and finding better ways to move are just as important to me.”

A spokesperson for the brand also said: " Robin represents performance, discipline and reliability, but also an active way of life that goes far beyond football.

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has become the company's latest ambassador (Image: ENGWE)

"Together, we want to make e-mobility a more natural part of everyday life and inspire more people to move, explore and enjoy every ride.”

Van Persie is yet to return to football after leaving Feyenoord, who hired his former Netherlands team-mate and ex-Rangers manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst as his successor.

He still has a firm connection to the club, with his son Shaqueel van Persie turning out for the Dutch giants. Last season, the ex-United forward was the one who gave Shaqueel his senior debut for the Rotterdam side.

View 3 Images Van Persie is yet to return to football (Image: 2026 Koji Watanabe)

When asked why he turned to his son, who is also a left-footed striker, during a 3-1 Europa League defeat to Celtic, Van Persie replied: "I made that call as a coach, not as a dad because we needed a goal.

"Shaqueel is a player who can score a goal from all angles. That was the reason I brought him on. From a father's point of view, when your son makes his debut that is always a special moment. But I wasn't that busy with enjoying that moment, I was doing my work like Shaqueel was."

Sports.title: Under-15s football chaos as police called when fight breaks out between adults and children
Sports.content:
Under-15s football chaos as police called when fight breaks out between adults and children

A junior football match in Wales descended into chaos as a brawl broke out on the sidelines, with adults and children getting involved in the altercation during a youth match

View Image Two men fight at a junior Welsh football match

Chaos broke out at an U15 match with both adults and children involved in a confrontation. The incident occurred during a match between Hakin United and Pennar Robins in Wales on Saturday.

‌



Footage shared shows two adult men on the pitch. A player then appears to kick towards one of the men as other individuals try to break up the fight.

‌



The confrontation continues on the sidelines. One appears to kick the other, who ends up on the ground.

‌



A number of adults and young players are subsequently seen wading in, while some of the stunned spectators — including young children — can be heard crying out "woah, woah" and "calm down".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Dyfed Powys Police and the West Wales Football Authority have now launched a formal investigation into the incident, with the governing body confirming in an official statement that the matter is being treated "extremely seriously", reports Wales Online.

‌



"The WWFA are aware of an incident which occurred at a junior football fixture in Pembrokeshire and of video footage circulating in relation to the matter," the statement read.

"The incident is being taken extremely seriously and will be considered in accordance with the appropriate disciplinary and safeguarding procedures, an investigation has commenced.

"As this process is ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further on the circumstances of the incident or any individuals involved at this stage.

‌



"The welfare and safety of all young players, coaches, officials and spectators remains of paramount importance, the appropriate action will be taken following the conclusion of the relevant processes."

A police statement read: "Dyfed-Powys Police received a report of a public order offence which took place at Hakin Football Club on Picton Road, Hakin, on Saturday (12/9).

"The incident was reported to have taken place at a time between 12pm and 12.30pm. The matter has been recorded and allocated for onward investigation."

Article continues below

A Pembrokeshire League spokesperson confirmed they were aware of the matter and that it had been referred to the WWFA "for appropriate action to be taken".

They went on to say: "Incidents like this are not commonplace within Pembrokeshire Football and we hope any punishment issued by the WWFA will deter any similar incidents from occurring."

A representative for Hakin United stated that the club was not in a position to comment further at this time, but emphasised that the protection of children remains the club's utmost priority.

Sports.title: Howard Webb sent unanimous Pro Ref verdict after Manchester derby VAR howler
Sports.content:
Howard Webb sent unanimous Pro Ref verdict after Manchester derby VAR howler

THE BIG DEBATE: The latest weekend of Premier League fixtures was marred by a host of controversial refereeing decisions and VAR calls with fans now debating whether it's time for more change at the top of Pro Ref

View 3 Images Howard Webb must now be questioned (Image: Getty Images)

It was a bad weekend to be a Premier League referee. It all started with the controversy at the Stadium of Light as Sunderland were awarded a penalty.

‌



The decision left Mikel Arteta furious and while it meant little in the end, the debate over the decision has rolled on. And then came the Manchester derby. Erling Haaland's goal was ruled out on the pitch, only to be given by a VAR intervention.

‌



The only problem was that it actually should have been chalked off, with Pro Ref forced into an embarrassing apology in the aftermath.

‌



It has left fans, coaches and players alike questioning the authority of Pro Ref and boss Howard Webb. So is it time for a major change at the top of refereeing?

Mirror Football writers have their say...

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Daniel Orme

In whatever guise Pro Ref or PGMOL or whatever it becomes next is in, there is always going to be debate around refereeing decisions in football. It’s why it’s the best game in the world.

And the old cliche is correct in what goes around comes around. One week a decision will go for you, the next it won’t. That’s just football.

‌



Does that make it right? No, not at all.

In my opinion, it’s not Pro Ref that needs a revamp, it’s the whole VAR system. Wayne Rooney is absolutely correct in his suggestions that it is sucking the delight and the spontaneity out of the game.

Managers should be able to choose when to appeal in a system similar to both rugby and cricket. Then, there would be no complaints over whether something has been checked or not.

‌



Putting the power in the hands of the players and those coaching them will go a long way to ironing these issues out. And you wouldn’t have got a situation like the one on Sunday.

Will that solve the competence of officials? Again, no. But you’d like to think that there’d be more developed and intelligent referees without having the crutch of VAR to lean on for every single decision they make.

View 3 Images Howard Webb must now be questioned (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Andy Dunn

A title such as Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL) could not get any less snappy so you have to admit Pro Ref has a far better ring to it.

The trouble is that the refereeing and VAR system needs more than a cosmetic overhaul. It reminds me of the time when authorities would tackle problem areas in their cities by renaming them. Roads would become boulevards, estates would become villages, and they thought that would do the trick.

Pro Ref needs a boss, a figurehead. Howard Webb has his moments of clarity but he cannot afford for there to be any more howlers like the one that gave City the win in the Manchester derby.

‌



And quite frankly, does the professional game need its head of refereeing to come out and explain the obvious? Some say yes, some think those explanations are useful.

But surely time would be better spent grafting away on exactly what went wrong.

The VAR official’s obvious mistake that led to United’s defeat should not mean the end of Webb’s tenure but a good refereeing boss should be the same as a good referee.

‌



You don’t notice him. And, right now, that its not the case with Webb.

John Cross

You can throw stats at us.

Fewer interventions, quicker checks and a better VAR return. And yet all good work is undone by the ridiculous farce of Erling Haaland’s goal at Old Trafford.

‌



When you have got everyone scratching their heads and wondering how the goal stood and yet the officials defied logic by ruling it was ok… then you have got serious problems.

It is embarrassing and highly damaging. Howard Webb is coming up for four years in the game. He communicates better, is way better as a leader than what we had before… but is it working?

The clubs don’t seem to think so. Look at what Michael Carrick said. Mikel Arteta the day before after his side were punished with a penalty against Sunderland.

‌



View 3 Images VAR interevened to give the goal at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Yes, they wanted to stop penalty box grappling. But this is always the case. Make a big song and dance, there is a crackdown in the first month when teams get penalised and then it evens out. How is that fair? How is that good leadership?

One game has a lighter touch on VAR. The next doesn’t. Honestly, it’s become a farce. No consistency. Any improvements get wiped out by high-profile errors and that has to be at Webb’s door.

‌



We have to get teams of officials, a better understanding and communication. And we must do it quick. This guessing game and lack of consistency is simply not good enough.

James Whaling

The decision was patently wrong and we would all rather see the back of VAR. But it's about time the finger was pointed higher up.

If the referees and VAR officials aren't up to scratch (although it's worth noting the on-field team got the decision right) then we need to start asking why?

‌



Howard Webb has been in charge of ProRef, formerly the much wordier Professional Game Match Officials Limited, for four years. He was tasked with smoothening VAR and making it a quicker, more accurate process. Can we honestly say he has succeeded?

Webb will appear on the box alongside Michael Owen in the next week or two explaining how his colleagues came to the wrong decision and offering platitudes about how they will try to avoid a similar incident in future.

But it will happen again. Make no bones about it. It has kept happening again for four years. We are only four games into the new season and we already have a clanger of a decision that could prove pivotal at the end of the season.

Article continues below

It's time for fewer words and more action. Things need to improve, sharpish, and if they don't Webb should stand aside for somebody else to have a go.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin and Leeds bully Newcastle in dominant victory
Sports.content:
Leeds United maintained their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign with a breathless 4-1 victory over Newcastle.

Both sides came into the game with five points on the board from the opening three games, but Matthias Jaissle's bubble was emphatically burst as he suffered a dramatic first defeat as Newcastle boss.

Without the electric Anthony Elanga, the visitors offered much less of a threat and could not handle the relentless press from the home side, led by the imperious Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Unfortunately he is injured. We need to investigate further and in more detail to find out how long he will be out. We will miss him and hope he is back to play quickly. It could be [long-term]. We hope not. He will get another MRI next week and we will see.

Leeds felt slighted when Matias Fernandez-Pardo, making his first start for his new club, avoided punishment for an alleged 'handball' inside the penalty area. That was soon forgotten as the hosts' dominance soon paid off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Newcastle's Matias Fernandez-Pardo avoids giving away an early penalty with a potential handball in the third minute.

There was an element of luck to their first, as Ao Tanaka's shot deflected off two Newcastle defenders with the last touch coming off Lewis Miley to wrong-foot Lukas Hornicek.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Miley's 'huge deflection' hands Leeds the lead against Newcastle.

That then led to the Calvert-Lewin show truly beginning. The striker thought he had his eighth career goal against the Magpies with a bullet header three minutes later. However, replays showed the ball had last come off team-mate Jayden Bogle, meaning he had to settle for the assist.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jayden Bogle gets the last touch on Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header as Leeds extend lead against Newcastle

The Leeds No 9 wasn't to be denied his next goal, bulldozing his way into the penalty area before calmly slotting home a third before the break.

The floodgates remained firmly open after half-time, with Noah Okafor adding a fourth - and the pick of the bunch. The forward produced a delightful weak-foot volley on the bounce, sending it arrowing into the bottom corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominic Calvert-Lewin gets his goal to give Leeds a three-goal lead against Newcastle

Bazoumana Toure grabbed a late consolation, but it did little to take the gloss off a thoroughly one-sided display. The result leaves Leeds sitting third at the end of the fourth round of fixtures - their highest position at this stage of a season since the 2000/01 campaign.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Noah Okafor makes it FOUR for Leeds against Newcastle with a super strike from Ethan Ampadu's throw-in.

The key moments from Elland Road

2: NO PENALTY! Fernandez-Pardo avoids conceding spot-kick for alleged ‘handball.’

14: SAVE! Hornicek makes a top drawer save from close range to deny Bogle.

25: SAVE! Bogle again threatens as he stings the palms of Hornicek with vicious attempt.

32: GOAL! Tanaka’s deflected strike comes off TWO Newcastle players before beating Hornicek.

35: GOAL! Two in three minutes as Bogle gets last touch from Calvert-Lewin's bullet header.

41: SAVE! Best chance of the half for Newcastle as Barnes is denied from close range.

45+1: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin can’t be stopped as he finally gets his goal.

59: GOAL! Okafor gets in on the act with stunning strike on the bounce.

89: GOAL! No clean sheet for Leeds as Toure adds late consolation.

Farke hails 'outstanding' Calvert-Lewin

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking with Sky Sports:

“I wasn’t happy that we allowed them to score one goal. But, it doesn’t take anything away from the fact that my boys were brilliant and we fully deserved to win the game. There’s no such thing as a perfect performance though, and this is one of the rare points I have to criticise.

“We have energy, quality, good structure in and out of possession. We have a good fitness level, also. It’s not just the will, otherwise whoever had the strong will would always win the game. We have to have the right triggers and everyone needs to be spot on. It’s lots of work on the training ground to be that compact and intense.

On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:

“He’s in outstanding shape and he plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group and he’s taken the responsibility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin reacts to having his goal taken away and awarded to Jayden Bogle against Newcastle.

“His work rate is top. It’s not just scoring the goals. The way he plays for us is outstanding. He’s definitely one of the stand out strikers in the league.”

Jaissle: We didn't match Leeds physically

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking with Sky Sports:

"That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said many times we will have ups and downs and challenges along the way. Tonight, we faced that challenge. It’s really tough. Difficult to digest, but this is a chance to learn because there’s not long until the next match at home to show the right reaction.

"You need to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against a physical and strong team. Leeds are so intense, especially at home and we couldn’t match that physicality in the first half. That was a key element. No excuses, we have to learn from it.

"Injuries are also a challenge that we need to overcome and will. This is the message I have given to the players. There will be no issue with confidence."

Carragher: Newcastle got beaten up

Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:

"Leeds are fifth in the Premier League table since December. That should make Newcastle feel better as it has been a bad night for them when the world was watching. They have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team.

Image: Leeds sit fifth in the Premier League since games from December 2025

"It will be a tough season at times for Newcastle with the manager and young players finding their feet in the Premier League. They just got beaten up."

On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:

"Calvert-Lewin was unplayable. One of the greatest sights in football is seeing a centre-forward rise above everyone and attack the ball.

"Look how high his legs are. I don't think there is a better player in the air in the Premier League."

Big learning curve for Jaissle

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie on X:

"That has to be a huge learning curve for Newcastle tonight. Looking at the team sheet for that opening game against Liverpool, with a midfield two and Yoane Wissa in the No 10, it looked like they were going to get overpowered.

"They didn't. Perhaps it was the emotion of the Kevin Keegan tributes, maybe it was because it was the opening game, or perhaps it was the Alexander Isak motivation. There was a lot going on that day.

Image: Matthias Jaissle suffered his first defeat as Newcastle boss

"But Leeds away on a Monday night, you need physicality & runners. Even a midfield three of Bruno Guimaraes-Sandro Tonali-Joelinton would find that a tough match tonight.

"Newcastle were bullied by Leeds' physicality and numerical advantage in the engine room.

"It's a long season, and it's been a very good start, but that's a real eye opener for the the new Newcastle manager."

Sports.title: Papers: Blundering VAR duo set to be blocked from officiating on Man Utd games
Sports.content:
The top stories and transfer rumours from Tuesday's newspapers...

Sports.title: McGregor criticises 'team of individuals' after Celtic's Old Firm collapse
Sports.content:
"You saw a team and a team of individuals."

Captain Callum McGregor was scathing in his assessment of Celtic's League Cup defeat to Rangers.

The Hoops travelled to Ibrox for a quarter-final tie against their Old Firm rivals unbeaten in seven domestic games this season.

And McGregor offered no excuses for the 3-0 defeat: "It wasn't us. The difference between the two sides was you saw a team and then you saw a team of individuals as well.

"Rangers were a team and you could see that.

"We looked like a team of individuals who like to do our own thing and play when we got the ball, not necessarily run when you don't have the ball when that's the thing you can't do when you come here.

"You can't defend with six players, it's impossible."

The cup exit comes after Celtic's Champions League qualifying defeat by Austrian side LASK, where they surrendered a 4-0 aggregate lead to be beaten 5-4.

Image: Celtic collapsed in the second leg of their Champions League qualifier against LASK

They host Hungarian side Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday before Rangers travel to Celtic Park in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

"We've put ourselves under pressure, we need to respond on Thursday and then we need to respond on Sunday but we very quickly need to get to the level," McGregor added.

"But trying to get the message to everyone that we have to be the team that we want to be.

"We need to find a way to do that quickly because we lost a big game against LASK and we lost another big game on Sunday and it's not acceptable.

"There'll be other big games throughout the season and eventually you have to win one if you want to be considered a good team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill reacts to their 3-0 defeat to Rangers in the League Cup quarter-finals

"If we want to be a good Celtic team then we'll have to win the big games. One thing we've always done is win big games and turned up when it mattered.

"So far this season we've been bitty in games and we need to fix it."

Image: Rangers beat Celtic in the first Old Firm of the season

With the memories of Austria still fresh in his mind, McGregor feared the defeat could have been even more damaging.

He said: "Yeah, you don't want fours and fives for sure.

"As soon as the goals go in, then I'm saying to Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales, no more goals.

"We need to just tighten this up. Of course we always want to get back in the game, we always want to be a team that, even at 3-0 down you still want to have a chance.

"But you have to understand the circumstances as well, well beaten at 3-0 with good goals against you, but if it starts to run at fours and fives then you're talking about a different ball game."

Sports.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
Sports.content:
The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.

It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.

The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

However, under a virtual or actual safety car, due to the speeds and geography of the layout, there was a chunky 12-second advantage in pitting under the safety car while rivals are travelling much more slowly. And that decided who would win the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.

The first-lap Madring melee

With so little circuit knowledge, especially for Lando Norris who had missed virtually a full practice session with car gremlins, and for others who had had sizeable shunts along the way, this meant that all three available tyre compounds were represented on the grid.

On the front row, pole sitter Norris, after a sensational qualifying lap, and fellow front-row sitter Kimi Antonelli had medium compounds. Max Verstappen was on soft compound tyres, like Lewis Hamilton. Others like Charles Leclerc's Ferrari and George Russell's Mercedes were on the hard compound tyres.

And that's how they set off. Norris got away reasonably well and aggressively covered off Antonelli. The young Italian would fail to slow enough, and bypass both of the two early chicanes, hitting the throttle hard through the run-off areas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli found himself going wide twice on the opening lap of the Spanish Grand Prix.

This meant he would clearly have to give back to Norris the lead he now had, but Verstappen read this very well, and using his speed, guile, and soft compound tyres, he would not let Antonelli simply hand the place back to Norris without helping himself to second place.

However, in the melee early after the start, Verstappen too had a straight run through a chicane, in his view to avoid a shunt with Hamilton.

In the view of the stewards however he had gained an unfair advantage and, much to Max's chagrin, his team told him, before the stewards did, to hand the place to Lewis which by now necessarily included Antonelli too.

It probably cost Max a victory in the end.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen FUMES over Red Bull team radio after being told to give position back to Lewis Hamilton after running off track in an incident at the first corner.

How the Virtual Safety Car turned the race Antonelli's way

Antonelli is definitely getting the rub of the green in this phase of the season, although it must be said that his speed and consistency have enabled him to make sure he doesn't waste these golden opportunities, and on lap 14 he would be handed another.

Norris had been flying out front, looking very assured. But when Lance Stroll lost his Aston Martin under braking and became marooned down one of the few and short run-off areas, it looked reasonably certain that there would be a virtual safety car to recover that.

Norris was fast approaching the pit-lane entry, the team didn't want to pit him on simply the chance of a safety car rather than the certainty, given how hard it was to overtake even significantly slower traffic if they didn't pit.

Just as the race director gave the VSC order, Norris had passed the pit entry. But his lead was over four seconds and, critically, Mercedes did have time to pit Antonelli. If only Lando hadn't been in such great form…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris admits team 'were too quick' after missing a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead.

Ferrari kept Leclerc out on his hard tyres, the relatively early safety car hurting his strategy. But clearing away stricken cars had been rather slow all event and might, just might, Norris be able to complete another lap at safety car speed and still get a cheap pit stop in?

Not at all. It went green and full racing speed when he was two corners from the pit-lane entry, and he then had to navigate the whole pit lane whist his main rivals were flat out. And to cap it all, McLaren delivered him a seven-second pit stop rather than the usual two seconds.

Undeterred, Lando set about catching up to Verstappen and Antonelli in fine fashion.

Leclerc would impressively lead until he pitted on lap 48 to park his tired hard tyres. If that sounds long, a very unimpressed Pierre Gasly was left out on track by his Alpine team for 55 of the 57 laps.

This all left Antonelli in the lead, but with Verstappen pushing hard as Norris was catching him, the three leaders were close together in the final stages.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater reflects on all the big talking points after a chaotic Spanish Grand Prix.

But there was no way past, and having led his 13th straight F1 race, Antonelli would now lead the championship by 81 points from his team-mate Russell. It's the fifth consecutive race where the 20-year-old Italian has extended his points lead.

Mercedes power units also won their 251st race in F1 history, tieing with Ferrari. Impressive numbers all round.

Russell in the other Merc was mighty fast too and would catch Leclerc but had to be content with following him home in fifth place, being a relative outlier on a two-stop strategy by pitting on laps 14 and 28.

It simply won't fall into place for George, he's not catching any breaks this season so far.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Sadly, Hamilton's Ferrari had brake issues in the opening laps and he would retire for the first time since Brazil last season. This meant Liam Lawson, standing in for the injured Isack Hadjar, grabbed eight more points in sixth place for Red Bull to go with Verstappen's excellent 18 for second place, in a car which wasn't second fastest.

The VSC rule debate and expectations of 2027 Madring change

Antonelli and Verstappen were both immediately magnanimous post-race when declaring it Norris' victory without the unfortunate virtual safety car timing. Should a driver lose a race because another driver has made a mistake or had a car failure?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory.

What goes around comes around in the course of a season and even a career, but it felt rather like a robbery on Sunday.

Some racing categories temporarily close the pit lane except for emergency repairs (or emergency refuelling if they have that), but that can all get a bit confusing and congested too in the pit lane and is still not equal for everyone.

One solution might be to ensure that if a virtual safety is deployed, then it must stay in place for at least a full lap of all the runners to keep it fairer. Although, of course, that costs green flag full-speed racing time, which is what people want to see in the grandstands and on their devices.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jude Bellingham talks Real Madrid's start of the season and F1 on Martin Brundle's Grid Walk.

By next year I hope and expect that the Madring will have some track layout changes to improve overtaking, a more condensed and practical set up behind the scenes, and better signage for all. It has all the ingredients to make a credible contribution to the F1 season.
