Sports.title: Carra: Arteta becoming like Sir Alex after ref criticism
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher says Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is "becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League" after strongly criticising the penalty awarded against his side in Saturday's 2-0 win at Sunderland.

A furious Arteta described the saved second-half penalty as "unacceptable" after referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa brought down Dan Ballard.

The Gunners have subsequently sought an explanation from refereeing body Pro Ref over the penalty award.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Was Ezri Konsa’s challenge on Dan Ballard enough for Sunderland to be awarded a penalty?

Arteta's anger has led Carragher to draw a comparison with ex-Manchester United boss Ferguson, who was famously unafraid to publicly criticise match officials, even while his side were the dominant domestic force.

Arsenal did not concede a penalty in last season's title-winning campaign and Carragher believes "don" Arteta is using his Premier League-champion status to influence referees' decision-making.

He told Monday Night Football: "This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now.

"He's the don at the moment; he's the Premier League champion.

"A lot of new managers about... he's been in his role for six or seven years, and he feels he's in a position of power to say, 'Yeah, it wasn't a penalty'. And I don't think it was a penalty.

"But it'd be interesting to see how long it takes for another referee to give a penalty against Arsenal in a similar situation.

"I thought it was very interesting in the press conference; one of the journalists made a point about, no matter what question you asked him, he kept going back to the penalty, so he was determined to get the narrative out that this won't happen again to his club.

"But that's a manager - we've seen it with Sir Alex Ferguson, we've seen it with Jose Mourinho."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League clash between Sunderland and Arsenal

Former Luton, Middlesbrough and Wolves boss Rob Edwards was the special guest on MNF and concurred with Carragher's view on Arteta.

He said: "I think Jamie's right. He's put himself into a position now where he's looking after his team and his football club, and people will listen to the Premier League-winning manager, won't they?

"They will listen to him; he's a powerful voice there now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Was Ezri Konsa’s challenge on Dan Ballard enough for Sunderland to be awarded a penalty?

Latest from Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Arsenal are set to hold talks with Pro Ref over the penalty Sunderland were awarded on Saturday.

The Gunners want an explanation for why the penalty was given on the field and then approved by VAR.

Arsenal have regularly asked Pro Ref for consistency in refereeing decisions.

Image: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta (left) was shown a yellow card in their win at Sunderland

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said at his post-match press conference at the Stadium of Light:

"The first question we have to discuss is this. This is not acceptable at this level.

"It was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium that was unbelievable.

"Sunderland are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that in a really difficult week.

"And on top of that, we have to go through what we have done today, that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

"I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"So I don't know what to think.

"I'm sad that we have to discuss this after such a beautiful game, that at this level, has the gravity of that. Because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

"At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

Sports.title: BMW PGA Championship: Field, format and prize money as McIlroy returns
Sports.content:
Which players could impress at the BMW PGA Championship? Will LIV Golf players feature? Who is playing in the Celebrity Pro-Am? We get you up to speed ahead of this week's DP World Tour event at Wentworth, live on Sky Sports.

What is the BMW PGA Championship?

The BMW PGA Championship is one of the flagship events on the DP World Tour calendar, with the tournament first being held in 1955.

It should not be confused with the BMW Championship, the second of the PGA Tour's two FedExCup Playoffs, with the BMW PGA Championship hosted annually in Surrey, England, each September.

Alex Noren returns as the defending champion after he defeated Adrien Saddier in a play-off at last year's tournament.

Where is the BMW PGA Championship played?

The tournament is hosted annually at Wentworth Club, one of England's most prestigious golf courses.

Wentworth was first opened as a golf club in 1922 and has since hosted some prestigious events, including the 1953 Ryder Cup and the AIG Women's Open in 1980.

Who can impress?

Some big names are set to tee up at Wentworth including two-time Masters champion Rory McIlroy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy wowed fans by chipping in for birdie on the opening hole of the 2025 BMW PGA Championship

The world No 2 won the BMW PGA Championship in 2014 and returns to Wentworth hoping to improve on a tied-41st place finish at the Amgen Irish Open. Despite dropping down the leaderboard, McIlroy said he was "encouraged" by certain aspects of his game coming into this week.

Patrick Reed has enjoyed a fine season on the DP World Tour since he left LIV Golf at the beginning of the year. The 2018 Masters champion currently leads the Race to Dubai Rankings and comes into the week off the back of an impressive tied-second finish at the Amgen Irish Open.

Prior to last weekend, Shane Lowry's last victory on the DP World Tour came at the BMW PGA Championship in 2022. But on Sunday, he carded a seven-under 63 to secure a staggering 11-shot victory at the Amgen Irish Open.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Fitzpatrick has enjoyed his most successful season on the PGA Tour in 2026, winning three events

Englishmen Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose are two other players who can impress this week. Fleetwood has four top-five finishes on the PGA Tour this season, notably placing tied-fourth at The Open at Royal Birkdale.

Rose has also enjoyed a great season on the PGA Tour, which included a victory at the Farmers Insurance Open and a tied-third finish at The Masters.

What LIV Golf players will feature at the BMW PGA Championship?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Rahm is one of multiple LIV Golf players in the field at Wentworth

Jon Rahm is one of multiple LIV Golf players in the field this week. This year the Spaniard clinched his third successive LIV Golf Individual Championship in August, and also finished tied for second at the PGA Championship in May.

His Legion XIII team-mate Tyrrell Hatton is also in the field this week. Hatton has enjoyed a great year at the majors, placing tied-third at The Masters and tied for seventh at the US Open, but arrives at Wentworth after missing the cut at the Amgen Irish Open.

What's at stake?

A £6.6m ($9m) prize purse is up for grabs this week at Wentworth. Last year's winner, Noren, took home a cash prize of £1.13m ($1.53m).

With this being a Rolex Series Event, a total of 8,000 Race to Dubai Rankings points are also up for grabs.

What is the Celebrity Pro-Am at the BMW PGA Championship?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gareth Bale, Tom Holland and Sir James Anderson have all played in the Celebrity Pro-Am in the past

Each year, Wentworth hosts a celebrity Pro-Am event featuring star-studded fields packed with big names from the sporting world and the entertainment industry.

This year is no different, with the DP World Tour having already announced that former Chelsea stars John Terry and Eden Hazard will both play in the event, alongside ex-Liverpool striker Robbie Fowler.

The BMW PGA Championship Celebrity Pro-Am is set to take place on Wednesday, the day before the tournament, with one professional player leading a team of amateurs in the competition.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin shows the way as Leeds thrash limp Newcastle and rise to third
Sports.content:
At what stage does a good start become something more significant? Perhaps we are not quite there yet; maybe we are. But as the goals flew in on a chaotic night at Elland Road, it was difficult not to think the boundaries of expectation for Leeds were potentially being redrawn.

Ask those close to the action over the summer at Leeds and the feeling was that there was a possibility of something special materialising this season. Having found their feet in the Premier League in the last campaign, the platform had been set and a very good summer transfer window seemed like the catalyst for even brighter days to return to West Yorkshire.

But even with that optimism in mind, this night felt significant. Leeds did not just beat a Newcastle side who themselves have started brightly under Matthias Jaissle, they dismantled them. And with the manner of this victory, Daniel Farke’s side sit third in the table.

Perhaps, in this world of demanding success overnight, there is a lesson here in patience for both clubs too. As Elland Road’s patrons likely pinched themselves when the outstanding Dominic Calvert-Lewin made it 3-0 before half-time it was easy to forget that, under a year ago, large swathes of supporter were suggesting time was up for Farke.

His decision to change to a back three against Manchester City last November saved his job and sparked an upturn in form that saw Leeds secure safety before starting this campaign in magnificent fashion. If this start continues with another win over Crystal Palace on Sunday, perhaps this side can do greater things than many first thought.

As for Jaissle, this was his first large bump in the road as Newcastle manager and there will possibly be more over the coming months as he imprints his vision on this team. But the decision-making of the Leeds side who vanquished them is evidence enough that patience can often pay off and Jaissle and his team could have no complaints about the scoreline.

Leeds were magnificent from start to finish. The opening goal was perhaps a touch fortuitous as Ao Tanaka’s shot bounced off the substitute Sean Steur and Lewis Miley to wrongfoot Lukas Hornicek, but it was the least Leeds deserved. Two minutes later, the lead was doubled when Jayden Bogle headed home a James Justin cross.

View image in fullscreen Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header for Leeds’ second was deflected in off Jayden Bogle. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Bogle has quietly been one of Leeds’ standout performers for some time and he is one of a few Leeds players who Thomas Tuchel may find difficult to ignore before naming his latest England squad later this week. The man who slotted home Leeds’ third in first-half stoppage time has perhaps even greater a claim for a call-up.

Calvert-Lewin’s latest goal was brilliantly taken; a measured finish that made it 3-0 at half-time.

With James Trafford between the sticks, Leeds have a clutch of players who may be fancy their chances of international recognition if they keep this up; a surefire sign of a club trending upwards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They may have a manager in that bracket as well. “There’s never a perfect performance in football but that was top class for more or less the whole game,” Farke said. “We know we have to stay humble; we might not have the best individual quality but we can be an outstanding team.”

The prospect of a grand Newcastle comeback appeared unlikely from the moment Sven Botman carelessly gave away possession to Anton Stach shortly after half-time and Stach spurned a glorious chance to make it 4-0. But Leeds did not have to wait long for their fourth goal, as Noah Okafor struck through a crowded penalty box to put the result beyond doubt.

Jaissle’s demeanour became more and more exasperated as the evening wore on and unsurprisingly he cut a frustrated figure afterwards. “We couldn’t match the intensity of Leeds and you see how difficult it can be to win a game in the Premier League,” he said. “We’ll have some ups and downs and this was a big down. A tough night.”

There was at least a consolation in the final moments as Bazoumana Touré, a bright spark after coming on, capitalised on a rare Leeds error to make it 4-1.

But the damage had long since been done – and the party among the home support by this time was already well under way.

Sports.title: VARs who wrongly confirmed Haaland’s goal at Manchester United are stood down
Sports.content:
The video assistant referee officials who allowed Erling Haaland’s winning goal in the Manchester derby on Sunday have been stood down. Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have been told by Pro Ref they have not received appointments for this weekend’s round of Premier League fixtures.

Howard Webb, the chief ­refereeing officer, took the decision with his management team after a review of the weekend’s action. Their availa­bility will be reconsidered after the international break.

Donohue was called on to check Michael Oliver’s decision to ­disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute goal for offside. Using semi-automated ­offside technology, Donohue was able to establish that the Manchester City striker was onside and he overturned ­Oliver’s call. But he failed to spot Enzo Fernández had ­influenced play from an offside position, an ­infringement which Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.

This is the first time officials have been made to stand down this season owing to an error. Donohue, an EFL referee since 2018, has taken charge of three Championship matches this season as well as his VAR work. His EFL profile says he has completed Pro Ref’s “Enhanced VAR ­Training Programme”. ­Antrobus is also an assistant referee in the ­Premier League and ran the line in the first three matchdays.

Quick Guide How do I 

Pro Ref acknowledged an “error of ­judgment” in the Haaland incident in a statement on Sunday night and is understood to have contacted ­Manchester United to explain the mistake.

Sports.title: Haaland goal should not have stood but VAR made the right call with Sunderland penalty | Chris Foy
Sports.content:
There was a disappointing outcome on a big decision in the Manchester derby and no one will feel it more than the video assistant referee, Matt Donohue. On Sunday night, Pro Ref confirmed that Donohue had made a mistake in allowing Erling Haaland’s goal in City’s 1-0 victory to stand when Enzo Fernández had been in an offside position.

When a VAR considers a decision such as this they start from the point at which the goal is scored and work backwards. Here, when Haaland scores, the flag is raised by the assistant referee for offside. The VAR automatically checked that on-field decision and used a semi‑automated system to show Haaland was onside. The decision was then made to overturn the call and award the goal.

Before Haaland scores, however, an offside Fernández, marked by Lisandro Martínez, has challenged for the crossed ball with a diving header. The VAR needs to look at this aspect and make a two-part assessment. The first question is: does Fernández make a clear attempt to play the ball? The second: did that action affect the ability of Martínez to defend the cross? In this case, the answer to both questions was yes. The goal should not have been awarded.

I think Donohue looked at the Fernández situation and did not recognise it was an offence. He is a highly skilled VAR but referees are human and the fact he has got it wrong will hurt. He will learn from it but I would defend the performance of referees more broadly this season.

We’re 39 games into the campaign and they have started really well. We’ve seen some very good examples of officials dealing with holding offences, the ball is in play for longer and referees are managing goal-kicks and throw‑ins too. More stuff is thrown at them every season to deal with.

In the game at Manchester United, Haaland’s goal wasn’t the only incident to cause debate with a real split of opinion on what sanctions should have been imposed. With regards to the coming together between Bruno Fernandes and Phil Foden, which led to the City player being sent off, I’ve heard two reds, two yellows and two dustings down.

View image in fullscreen Patrick Dorgu plays the ball to Erling Haaland with Enzo Fernández clearly offside. Photograph: Sky Sports

Let’s be clear: Foden sticks his studs into Fernandes’s midriff after the United captain had kicked at him with a toe. Michael Oliver shows Foden a deserved red card for violent conduct. Fernandes had provoked Foden by moving his right toe into Foden’s backside but in my opinion, had Oliver seen it, he would have given Fernandes a yellow card because it was a pretty petulant act of unsporting behaviour. Whereas Foden’s kick was violent conduct, I would argue Fernandes’s was not.

The laws on violent conduct describe when a player “uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball”. Did Foden use excessive force or brutality against an opponent? I think he did. But Fernandes didn’t. There was no brutality in that. There was no force. Clearly, the referee didn’t see the act of petulance but in terms of the bigger decision the officials got it correct. Even Enzo Maresca said in his press conference that Foden was rightly sent off.

The previous day there was another incident with lots of noise around it: the decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal. Dan Ballard and Ezri Konsa go to ground in the Arsenal box and the verdict from John Brooks was penalty kick. You could quite clearly see that Konsa was holding Ballard and really focusing only on his opponent and not the ball. The VAR, Stuart Attwell, then checked the decision and had to determine whether the referee made a clear and obvious error.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ballard has got a little bit of Konsa’s shirt too and there’s a bit of tugging but that in itself, with all the bits and bobs going on, doesn’t jump out as a clear and obvious error, so they stay with the on-field decision. What is important to note is the light touch from VARs this season.

Lots of people will say penalty. Others will say not for me. Attwell was right to say check complete, confirming the penalty. If a penalty hadn’t been awarded, however, there would have been no intervention either because it’s not a clear and obvious error. It’s what we would term a check complete either way.

Chris Foy is a former Premier League referee

Sports.title: De Zerbi backs ‘sensitive guy’ Solanke to find form before tricky Anfield trip
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has no doubt Dominic Solanke will rediscover his best levels as the head coach made clear he had left no stone unturned in the mission to solve Tottenham’s goalscoring problem.

Spurs go to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after the 0-0 home draw with Everton in the Premier League on Saturday; they have not found the net in their four matches in the competition. Tottenham did beat Charlton 5-1 at home in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Solanke is the only forward in De Zerbi’s squad to have enjoyed a prolific season in England’s top division; he scored 19 times for Bournemouth in 2023-24, which convinced Tottenham to pay £55m for him. The 29-year-old has 22 additional goals in the Premier League, 12 of them for Spurs. De Zerbi has Omar Marmoush, who scored seven times in the league for Manchester City in the second half of 2024-25 after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt in January. That apart, the pickings for De Zerbi’s attacking players have been slim in the competition.

Solanke, whose pre-season was undermined by an injury sustained on the club’s tour of New Zealand and Australia, was ineffective against Everton and a target for criticism is some quarters. De Zerbi will keep the faith. He remembers being amazed at how well Solanke played for Bournemouth against his Brighton team in September 2023. Brighton won 3-1 but Solanke scored. De Zerbi knows that when Solanke is fully fit the goals and performances will follow. He intends to involve the former Liverpool striker at Anfield, whether from the start or as a substitute.

“Dom is a sensitive guy,” De Zerbi said. “He needs to feel full confidence – and from myself, he has big, big confidence. I believe he can score 10-15 goals, for sure. He’s already scored in Bournemouth so why not he can score in Tottenham? It’s the same sport.

“[He is] sensitive because he’s a smart guy. Sensitive guys are smart. Maybe [he has had] many injuries, maybe he doesn’t feel in the best physical condition, maybe he would like to do something different on the pitch. But now he’s not fit yet. He has to play. It can be important for him [at Anfield]. And then I think he comes back to the player who was in Bournemouth. I remember Brighton v Bournemouth in the Amex Stadium; he was incredible. I said to my assistant: ‘Who is this striker?’”

View image in fullscreen Dominic Solanke scores Tottenham’s second goal in their 5-1 Carabao Cup second round victory over Charlton. Photograph: John Walton/PA

De Zerbi continues to try to bond his players away from the pitch. He said he had again taken them for dinner in Mayfair last week and paid the bill. “As long as I keep some money for my cigarettes, then no problem,” he said with a smile.

De Zerbi is leaning heavily into video analysis, going through clips from matches in team meetings and giving the players individual ones to study. There has been an emphasis in training on attacking crosses in the right way and regaining possession in the final third. The players have also stayed behind for extra shooting practice of their own volition, De Zerbi said.

“If we want to change from the last two or three seasons we have to be stronger here,” he said, pointing to his head. “We have to believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. Or we change. You can change players or change coaches … change, change, change and nothing changes. Or you stay with the head, stay humble and with the right spirit to work. I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.”

De Zerbi reported that Sandro Tonali would miss the Liverpool game with a knock, and Richarlison will not be involved despite being eligible for the Carabao Cup; the Brazilian forward was omitted from Spurs’ Premier League squad.

Pedro Porro is still out but Destiny Udogie is back, and Mohammed Kudus is ready to start. James Maddison, though, is still unavailable. De Zerbi will make changes and he mentioned Marcos Senesi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Ben Davies, Lucas Bergvall and Mathys Tel as being in contention to come into the XI. Spurs have not won at Anfield in 17 matches.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool forwards they must do more to make his system work
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has shifted the focus on to Liverpool’s forwards for the team’s uninspiring display against Fulham, insisting they need to give more to make his system work.

The head coach admitted his team took “a step backwards” with their goalless draw on Saturday. His central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai struggled to contain their Fulham counterparts, winning two of five duels and one of nine duels respectively. But Iraola believes the problems started further forward with the pressing of Liverpool’s expensively assembled attack.

“It’s not a matter of just the midfielders,” he said. “When we have been good collectively the mid­fielders have looked a lot better and recovered more balls. It’s not because they are winning duels that they play better, it’s because we are helping them more to win the duels.

“If the ones up front do their job very well then the defenders and midfielders look good. If we are allowing them to defend one v one all the time and we are not aggressive, then our defenders will also struggle. If the players ahead of you are doing their job then you look a better midfielder or defender because you win more easier duels, you have more chance of winning one. It is more collective.

“It isn’t about changing this player for that player. That’s the help we have to give to our defenders and midfielders so everyone looks better, looks smarter and are in better positions.”

Iraola is unlikely to field the same frontline of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Víctor Muñoz when Tottenham visit Anfield in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday. Trey Nyoni is pressing for a start in midfield and Iraola confirmed that Giorgi Mamardashvili, whom he tried to sign for Bournemouth, would replace ­Alisson in goal.

View image in fullscreen The Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili will make his first appearance of the season in the Carabao Cup tie against Tottenham. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images

On the issues of Saturday, which contributed to a third draw in four Premier League games, he also said: “Compared to previous games, we won the ball a lot lower in the pitch. We don’t concede a lot, and the only big chance we conceded was our goal‑kick that we messed up. But we were recovering the ball always very low and when that happens you have to attack against 11 players and that makes it more difficult to make the difference.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In previous games we could win it a lot higher and use our quick transitions to attack against less players and use the space better. That is key to our system. We need to recover the ball as high as possible because it makes the offensive side a lot easier, and we have more situations to attack in one v one.”

Sports.title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
Kiat Lim wanted to see Valencia play so badly, so that is what he did. It was week four in La Liga, 6 September, and for the first time since he was given the presidency 18 months earlier, the owner’s 33-year-old son was going to watch his team play a competitive game. He was going to do it from the inside, too, so he took a flight to Spain, landing at Manises in a black mask and cap, a van to the hotel, then the team bus to Mestalla. He looked through the window as they rolled along Avenida Suecia, a huge, noisy crowd waiting, but when he got off and headed through the iron gate with its ornate club badge, he saw that this was no welcome.

Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat.

He had seen supporters leave early, seen those that stayed turn towards him, chanting for him and his family to leave for good. He had seen the hankies come out and his players head into the tunnel heads bowed. He heard his manager insist that they were hurt but not sunk. What he did not see – what no one had seen yet but everyone would see soon enough – was the verdict from the bench.

Withdrawn after an hour to a standing ovation, the World Cup winner Rodri took a towel and turned to Pau Cubarsí. “This lot are very weak, eh?” Spain’s captain said. “Very weak, mate. Very bad.” He asked where they finished last season, pulled a face that said seriously?! when he was told just outside Europe, and noted that they had not left their own half. Valencia, he said, were malísimo. Awful.

View image in fullscreen Rodri was caught on camera calling his former club ‘very weak’. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

The sequence was caught on camera by El Día Después, and soon it was everywhere. Rodri called Valencia’s captain José Luis Gayà, saying sorry. After Barcelona’s Champions League win against Feyenoord three days later, he offered a public apology. It was, the Valencia coach, Carlos Corberán, said, a touch of self-preservation about his reaction, the least Rodri could do: apology accepted but his “unfortunate” words had “not been born of respect”. Yet there was no taunt, no mocking, no derision, no sign of a smile; instead there was a kind of shocked sadness. His words had not been thrown in anyone’s faces and were not for sharing. They were also true.

And if Corberán noted that “Mestalla had applauded him too”, an aggravating factor, some of them would do it again: it had needed saying. Within a few days someone had designed T-shirts declaring: “They’re very bad.” Underneath it read: “We’re all Rodri.” They had barely started printing off before Corberán was gone. Shoot the manager, not the messenger.

Barcelona’s victory over Valencia last Sunday was the third time in four games that they had scored five. Three days later they did it again. But those were not really the same – at Mestalla it was hard to avoid the feeling that Hansi Flick’s side could have scored 10 if they wanted to – and this was not just about Barcelona, this was about them. Valencia really are malísimo. Four games into season, they had conceded nine and scored one – and that was a gift, scored by a man who is now seriously injured. They had a solitary point, were bottom, and things were not about to get any better. This Friday, they lost the Used To Be Big Derby, 1-0 to Sevilla at the Sanchez Pizjuan, Juan Iglesias’s header condemning Valencia to the worst start in their history and Corberán to the sack.

There is something about these two; the last two times Sevilla fired their manager (García Pimienta and Matías Almeyda), it was after defeat to Valencia, while this is the third time Valencia fired a coach having lost at the Sánchez-Pizjuán: Quique Sánchez Flores in 2007, Nuno Espírito Santo in 2015 and now Corberán. Sánchez Flores got sacked at 4am. This time the wait was a little longer, if not much. When Valencia’s players and staff got back to Paterna to collect their cars in the small hours of Saturday, 100 fans waited to shout abuse and by the time training had finished there on Sunday morning the decision was made. Corberán was told during a video call from Singapore, Lim 10,000km away again.

The coach who arrived in December 2024 with Valencia in the relegation zone and pulled them up to 12th; the manager who saw them slip into the relegation zone again at the halfway stage last season only to pull clear all the way to the edge of Europe, would not get the chance to try again. Just five weeks into the season, two months after his contract was extended for another year, and 10 days after the CEO, Ron Gourlay, insisted that stability meant standing by a coach he believed in even if fans, some players and an increasingly belligerent media might not, he was gone.

Mind you, Gourlay has gone too. At that defiant two-hour, via-translator press conference Gourlay insisted that if his critics were going to wait for him to go, their coffee would get cold, but he has been sacked along with all his staff. Braulio Vázquez, has joined from Osasuna – even though Braulio recently said Osasuna are the “only real club left” – given the task of finding a new coach, with the B team manager taking over for the time being. His arrival ushers in a restructuring and a “new era” at Valencia, the statement said.

Quick Guide La Liga results Show Sevilla 1-0 Valencia Racing Santander 2-1 Alavés Osasuna 0-2 Espanyol Athletic Bilbao 1-1 Elche Real Madrid 4-1 Rayo Vallecano Celta Vigo 1-1 Málaga Levante 2-4 Barcelona Getafe1-1 Deportivo A Coruña Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Braulio knows the club – he was sporting director there between 2011 and 2013 and his son is the left-back – and has been successful at Osasuna, widely considered a more convincing candidate than the man who was there until Sunday afternoon. Few fans are sorry to see Corberán go: in fact they have been chanting for just that, the social fracture another factor. A change of coach can change things, a change of CEO or sporting director too. Look at Valencia’s squad and they should and probably will be better than this, the academy keeps producing talent, and Mestalla still fills weekly. There are coaches out there that would convince, with Ernesto Valverde and Jagoba Arrasate’s names the first to be floated. They certainly couldn’t be much worse than they have been so far. But patience is thin and faith thinner, a pessimism long since having crept in, and not unjustifiably so.

The only thing most fans want of the owners now is for them to leave which plays a part too, everyone caught in the never-ending tension. It is less than two years since Gourley took over, a year since Lim said that they have a “proper sporting plan now ... which is not to say we did not in the past but now we have professionals in place.” He was already the sixth man to supposedly have responsibility for signings since Peter Lim bought the club in 2014. Óscar Sánchez will be Valencia’s fifteenth coach since then – and even Voro, the eternal caretaker who has had the job six times does not want it any more. Only Nuno and Marcelino have better win percentages than Corberán. This summer, they spent €9m (£7.7m); 13 clubs spent more. More than 20 players have come in and gone out in the last two years. Over the last seven seasons they have spent short of €70m; they have sold for more than €230m.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Corberán was sacked by Valencia after their worst start to a season in their history. Photograph: Fran Santiago/Getty Images

There was a line in Rodri’s apology that talked about context and context is everything: Valencia being bad was not one Sunday; the fear is that it’s any given Sunday, that the days when they were good may be gone. He said that his comments were born of surprise, sadness, but the saddest thing is many weren’t surprised at all. This is what it is, they thought, grateful that someone else said it; forgive them if they do not foresee a way out. Yet if ambition must be adjusted it is hard not to hold on to what you were, your identity still, and maybe that’s a problem too. The Valencia Rodri returned to is not the Valencia he left behind. The year he went to England, they were a Champions League team; they have not made Europe since. And on Sunday he was right, Corberán taking the fall within a week.

“We all want Valencia to get back to where they should be, one of the best clubs in our league,” Rodri said three days later, but he had already said enough, a truth told. Sitting in the stands, Lim had just about seen enough too.

Sports.title: European football: Inter roar back to beat Udinese and join Roma at the top
Sports.content:
Inter fought back ⁠from two goals down ​to beat Udinese 5-3 on Monday, maintaining their perfect Serie A start alongside Roma, who won 2-0 at Torino before Saturday’s match between ⁠the joint leaders. Both sides have 12 points from four matches and share top spot before their encounter at the Stadio Olimpico, while Como are third on 10 points ⁠after beating Parma 2-1.

Udinese stunned Inter with two goals in the opening 16 minutes, as James Abankwah headed home ​unmarked after nine minutes before Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled ‌the visitors’ lead with a ‌close-range finish seven minutes later. Inter hit back through Carlos Augusto, whose long-range effort flew into the bottom corner, ‌before Nicolò Barella levelled 10 minutes before half-time.

The champions completed the turnaround in the 59th minute when Marcus Thuram netted from inside the box after Andy Diouf’s cutback from the byline. Francesco Esposito added a fourth and Ange-Yoan Bonny made it 5-2 with 11 minutes remaining. Udinese pulled one back in stoppage time through Idrissa Gueye, but it proved no more than a consolation.

There was an injury concern for Inter as John Stones limped off with an apparent hamstring injury just after the hour mark. The England centre-back was making his first start after joining on a free transfer this summer.

The Inter manager, Cristian Chivu, confirmed Stones would have to be fully assessed to determine the extent of the issue. “I don’t know, I haven’t had a chance to talk to him,” Chivu told Dazn. “I think he felt something on his flexor [muscle], and he will probably need to get some tests done.”

View image in fullscreen Roma scorers Niccolò Pisilli and Donyell Malen celebrate at the final whistle. Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPA

Roma made it four ‌wins from four thanks to goals from Donyell Malen and Niccolò Pisilli at Torino. Malen broke the deadlock five minutes before the interval after ​pouncing on a misplaced pass from goalkeeper Lucas Perri that had been intercepted by Paulo Dybala. Pisilli wrapped up the win in stoppage time, firing home from an angle after Gianluca Mancini kept the ball in play near the byline.

The Roma coach, Gian Piero Gasperini ,praised the understanding between Malen and Dybala. “Clearly, these are two players who are very talented ⁠individually, but they also complete each other as a pair. They combine beautifully ​to create goals in many games,” ​he told Dazn Italia.

Como followed up their winning Champions League debut against RB Leipzig with a 2-1 home win over Parma, with Jacobo Ramón and Kaiki Bruno scoring for Cesc Fàbregas’s side. “This is an important victory for me as a coach, because I am starting to realise what team we could become,” Fàbregas said.

View image in fullscreen Natan (centre) and his Real Betis teammates fought back from 1-0 down to beat Villarreal 2-1. Photograph: José Jordan/AFP/Getty Images

Meanwhile in Spain, Real Betis secured a 2-1 win at Villarreal to move third in La Liga and leave their opponents in the relegation zone. Goals from Cucho Hernández and Natan helped Betis claim three points and pull level with Real Madrid, after Gerard Moreno opened the scoring for the home side.

“Right now everything’s going against us, teams are punishing us,” Moreno told Movistar. “We have to stick together and demand more of ourselves … maybe when we go behind, anxiety kicks in and it’s more difficult. It’s hard to explain [how few] points we have... we have to be a team now more than ever.”

Sports.title: PSG have finally won a game in Ligue 1 – but they were far from convincing
Sports.content:
It was just a flicker. Ferran Torres picks the ball up and passes it to João Neves. The Portugal midfielder plays it into Ousmane Dembélé, who has lured in Raphaël Le Guen and eliminates him with a mesmeric first-time back-heel into the path of Torres.

The Brest defence are just cones in a training drill, mere extras in this work of art as the Spaniard glides back into the scene to pass the ball into Egil Selvik’s bottom-left corner from 25 yards; it happened in slow motion, but was too quick for the Norwegian goalkeeper to react.

It is a move that had the slick and elegant fluidity of what we have come to expect from Paris Saint-Germain. Just four minutes in, the champions were ahead and the Stade Francis Le-Blé anticipated a show of force, a statement from their visitors.

Luis Enrique had described PSG’s start to the Ligue 1 season as catastrophic. A comfortable 6-1 win against Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League last Wednesday signalled a welcome return to form. The Sopposition manager, none other than Yaya Touré, described his opponents on the night as a machine – we have heard that before.

But once again, PSG were defective in Brittany on Sunday night, even if they did leave with all three points. Torres’s sublime finish was the only goal of the game. It was the Spaniard’s sixth since joining from Barcelona in the summer. All of his six efforts on target this season have found the net. He is clearly still riding the crest of a wave of confidence, having scored the winner in the World Cup final.

Torres’s supreme confidence is not shared by his teammates. Vitinha in particular has yet to resurface since the summer break and PSG are suffering from the lack of incision he usually provides. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not quite back to his usual levels either and going into this game, there were creeping doubts about Matvey Safonov in goal. The Russian was at fault last weekend when Stanis Idumbo finished at his near post to secure a win for Monaco. It was at his near post he conceded to Kai Havertz in the Champions League final in May; if there is a weakness in PSG, Safonov was the most likely candidate.

But it is only thanks to him that PSG ended a run of five games without a win against French opponents. He was not forced into action when Nuno Mendes played Kamory Doumbia in one-on-one in the second half, the Mali international striking the outside of the PSG post.

Safonov did get a strong hand down low to his left when Doumbia rose highest to thunder a header towards goal and in the dying stages Pathé Mboup’s curled effort to the far post was tipped around the corner.

View image in fullscreen Goalkeeper Matvey Safonov kept PSG in the game with a number of saves. Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty Images

Brest finished with a higher xG than the European champions, but had no points to show for it. Moments of brilliance in both areas were the difference. But that is what PSG are confined to at the minute: moments, flickers of brilliance.

“It was the worst of our four Ligue 1 matches, even if we won,” said Luis Enrique. “In the other three matches, we showed a high level at the back, but our opponents scored every chance. This time, it was the opposite.”

Alarm bells are not ringing. PSG often start slowly and it is only the quality of opposition faced at the start of the last campaign that ensured there was not such a significant deficit to the leaders. They are five points behind Lille, Monaco and Rennes, all of whom are on 10 points.

Last week, Marquinhos said that it was “a matter of ambition and motivation” as PSG hoped to replicate the success of the past two seasons. Just like Torres’s passed finish, PSG are all about timing and they have a knack for peaking at the right moment.

There were no doubts Brest were up to the occasion. The Stade Francis Le-Blé was a cauldron of emotion as Eric Roy was commemorated. The Brest manager, who guided the club into European competition for the first time, in 2024, died in June due to pancreatic cancer that began when he was appointed as the club’s manager in January 2023. His diagnosis was never made public.

Roy’s daughter, Victoria-Rose, spoke on the pitch before the match, “King Eric” shirts were worn on the sidelines and there were further moments of commemoration in the stands throughout the game. Hugo Magnetti said they had played for Roy. “He would have been proud of us, but he would have also ticked us off for missing some big chances.”

The game, at times, felt like a subplot, but what happened in it was not inconsequential. Some of those fears about waning “ambition and motivation” were deepened, as was a crisis of confidence among some of PSG’s key players, despite victory. But there were also flickers of brilliance Luis Enrique must hope will become more enduring as the season progresses.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Lille 2-0 Troyes Le Mans 2-2 Lens Brest 0-1 PSG Strasbourg 1-1 Monaco Auxerre 1-0 Nice Le Havre 0-0 Angers Lorient 2-2 Toulouse Paris FC 0-0 Lyon Rennes 1-0 Marseille Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Will Still and Auxerre have their first points on the board thanks to their young English forward Cameron Archer. The Southampton loanee made his debut last weekend and scored a stunner in a 3-1 defeat to Lyon. This weekend he scored the only goal of the game against Nice. The win drags Auxerre off the bottom of the table – a place now occupied by their opponents on the day. Nice, without a win, have scored once in their first four matches. Their coach, Olivier Pantaloni, says there are traces of last season’s difficult campaign lingering in the minds of his players. They must quickly dispel them in order to avoid a repeat.

Four games in and the temperature is already rising in Marseille. The season started well, with a 4-0 home win to Strasbourg on opening day, but they have since lost to Monaco, Paris FC and Rennes. There is no real shame in any of those defeats; the matches were close and the opponents are expected to be in the race for Europe. “We can rival these teams but not yet beat them,” said Bruno Génésio after the 1-0 defeat at Rennes on Friday. Génésio added it was not up to him to state the club’s objectives this season – a clear message to his superiors. “We may need to explain things more clearly Maybe we have to say it so that people can understand.” The lack of quality and depth in the squad says enough; Marseille are outsiders in the race for European football.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: John Stones devastated as he suffers nightmare first start for Inter Milan
Sports.content:
John Stones devastated as he suffers nightmare first start for Inter Milan

John Stones' first start as an Inter Milan player didn't end how he would have wanted it to, as he picked up an injury.

The England international asked to be substituted in the 62nd minute of Inter's 5-3 win over Udinese on Monday.

2 Stones had to be substituted after pulling up with a suspected muscle injury Credit: Reuters

He pulled up when chasing down ex-Watford striker Keinan Davis and was unable to carry on in the Serie A clash.

It was only his fourth appearance since joining the Italian giants, coming off the bench in all of his previous three games.

But after finally getting a start, Stones was withdrawn early after sitting down on the pitch and eventually walking off.

There has been no confirmed diagnosis of the injury from Inter yet, but reports in Italy suggest it is a hamstring injury for the former Manchester City man, which will be hugely worrying.

Stones' injury nightmare

Stones' last two years at Man City were hugely impacted by injuries, as he missed a whopping 58 games for club and country.

After multiple foot issues during the start of the 2024/25 campaign, he went on to suffer a hamstring issue in February 2025.

That saw him sit out for three months and miss 18 games, and followed three other hamstring issues across 2022 and 2023.

Then, after returning in 2025/26, Stones spent another two weeks on the sidelines with a muscle injury last September.

And a 67-day absence followed in December, as a thigh problem ruled him out for another 18 Man City matches.

He came back into the City fold in February but then sat out again from March to April with a calf injury, and now he could be set for another spell in the treatment room with Inter.

2 Stones has played four times for Inter Milan but he's already picked up an injury Credit: Getty

What games could John Stones miss?

If Stones is ruled out with another injury, he may not play again for Inter until October 10 against Parma.

A clash against Roma is coming up in Serie A on Saturday evening before the international break begins.

But the 32-year-old centre-back may not be in action for England during the break now, after picking up an issue.

The Three Lions take on Spain, Czechia and Croatia from September 26 through to October 3 in the new extended schedule.

That could be a big blow for Stones, as his future place in the squad may end up being threatened.

He played four games for England at the World Cup this summer, but there are plenty of other, younger options.

Tuchel will announce his squad this Friday, with confirmation of Stones' injury likely deciding whether he is included or not.

Sports.title: Newcastle labelled ‘naive’ by ex-manager as Matthias Jaissle slammed for ‘massive mistake’
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle made a critical selection error in his Newcastle United midfield as they were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United.

That's the view of talkSPORT host Adrian Durham, with former boss Steve Bruce also highlighting their lack of defensive judgement on a night to forget at Elland Road.



3 Newcastle shipped four goals on a bleak night in Leeds Credit: AFP

A chaotic period which saw three goals get scored in 14 minutes meant Newcastle were all but downed by the break on Monday night.

A Lewis Miley own goal was met with finishes from Jayden Bogle and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, before Noah Okafor wrapped it up for Leeds by the hour mark.

Newcastle, who scored a late consolation via Bazoumana Toure, were dealt an early blow when Nico Gonzalez went off on 19 minutes through concussion, with summer signing Sean Steur replacing him.



However, Durham did not understand the decision from Jaissle, hinting that his midfield duo lacked experience given they have played in a combined 63 league matches - 59 of which are from Miley.

"Nico Gonzalez has had to go off," he explained on talkSPORT. "Okay, fair enough, as he's already got Lewis Miley out there at 20 years old.



"He put Sean Steur on with him in central midfield, 18 years old. He's got Jacob Ramsey sitting on the bench who's 25 and over 150 Premier League appearances, and these two babies in centre mid are being exposed badly because he's maintained the four up front.

"I think it's a massive managerial coaching mistake from Jaissle. I don't get it."



Jaissle told talkSPORT afterwards that, although he was named on the bench, Ramsey could not play, saying: "He felt his thigh during the warm up so that was a reason why there weren't too many alternatives actually for that position.

"In general we trust the young lads but we also saw that they need time."

'Naive' Newcastle at Leeds

Bruce agreed with Durham and then took issue with the Newcastle back line as they extended their conceded goals tally to eight.

3 Durham and Bruce believe Jaissle got his team selection wrong Credit: Getty



"It's certainly bold in his selection that's for sure and it's bold in the selection throughout. The no.10 for example, they're not dropping in and playing a no.10.

"They're playing two out and out centre forwards and they've got two out and out wide players which leaves the middle of the pitch and they're trying to press the ball high up the pitch.

"They're a little bit naive in the whole defensive outlook of what they're trying to achieve. It looks great when it comes off and but when it goes badly wrong it's awful to experience because they've just been so naive.

"And you're right about youngsters. I mean, they've also got Joe Willock, who's had a really good start to the season.



"He's sitting on the bench too. I do believe if you're coming to somewhere like Leeds and go out and out attack, play two centre forwards and two wide players. For me it's a very, very big call."

Jaissle suffers first Newcastle defeat

Since replacing Eddie Howe just 18 days before their league opener, Jaissle has endured a positive start to life at Newcastle.

3 Newcastle have been dealt their first defeat of the season Credit: Getty

Three wins and from six in all competitions has come after a summer of upheaval that saw Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes all leave.



A 2-2 draw against Liverpool and 2-0 win at Tottenham Hotspur are among these results, but Jaissle's unbeaten run is now over.

The loss is Newcastle's first against Leeds in the Premier League since January 2021, ending a six-match streak.

It has put them 12th in the table with just one win and a sole clean sheet from four.

Newcastle were hit with blow in attack ahead of kick-off as it was revealed that Anthony Elanga has picked up an injury.



"Unfortunately, he is injured," Jaissle said. "We need to investigate further and in more detail to find out how long he will be out.

"We will miss him and hope he is back to play quickly. It could be (long-term).

"We hope not. He will get another MRI next week, and we will see."

The Carabao Cup has given Newcastle the most success this season as they have beaten West Brom and Millwall to reach the fourth round.

Newcastle will learn their opponents during the draw on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Europa League team bizarrely forced to stay in another country for away game due to hotel shortage
Sports.content:
Europa League team bizarrely forced to stay in another country for away game due to hotel shortage

Rennes have been forced to stay in a completely different country from where their Europa League opener will be played this week.

The Ligue 1 side are taking on Austrian outfit Sturm Graz in their first match of the campaign, but they're having to stay in Slovenia.

1 Rennes are having to stay at a hotel in Slovenia for their match in Austria Credit: AFP

The game, which is being played on Wednesday evening, is taking place at the same time as the MotoGP Grand Prix in Styria.

And that has led to the area expecting a huge number of people, who are going to be spending a few nights in hotels.

So, those hotels have all been fully booked up, and it seems Rennes had not planned far enough ahead...

Why are Rennes staying in Slovenia?

talkSPORT's European football expert Andy Brassell explained on Hawksbee and Jacobs on Monday: "Rennes are not even able to stay in Austria as they've completely run out of hotels.

"They're having to stay in Slovenia and get the bus to the game."

According to L'Equipe, Rennes are spending three days there for a training camp ahead of their Europa League clash.

The squad will then fly straight back after the match to prepare for their next league fixture against Lyon on Sunday.

Rennes are staying in Maribor, which is just an hour away from the Merkur Arena in Graz, despite being in a different country.

And it does mean they're going to have to get a coach to the game, travelling into Austria from Slovenia.

The game will take place on Wednesday at 8pm UK time.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich tipped to go after struggling Premier League striker as future Harry Kane replacement
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich tipped to go after struggling Premier League striker as future Harry Kane replacement

Bayern Munich have been tipped to target Nick Woltemade as Harry Kane's surprise successor.

Kane is still banging in the goals for the time being, becoming the fastest player to 100 goals for Bayern, but at 33 the Ballon d'Or contender is heading towards the back end of his career.



2 Kane opened his Bundesliga account for the season with the winner for Bayern against Elversberg on Sunday Credit: Getty

And European football expert Andy Brassell reckons the German giants will eventually sign Woltemade, despite the striker's struggles at Newcastle.

Germany international Woltemade joined Newcastle from Stuttgart last summer, just before Alexander Isak left for Liverpool, and scored eight Premier League goals in his first season with the Magpies.

However, he found net just twice between the turn of the year and the end of the campaign and has since been loaned out to Juventus.



Bayern 'convinced' Woltemade would join before

Still only 24, Woltemade is theoretically yet to hit his prime years, and Brassell believes he'll make his way back to the Bundesliga with Bayern one day.

"I still think Woltemade will end up at Bayern at some point," he told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs.



"They were convinced he would go there before Newcastle and he's had a difficult start at Juventus as well... quite a messy situation.

"They're trying to reform the front part of their team and they've ended up with this front pairing of him and Randal Kolo Muani.



"They were really out of nick in the back end of last season. It's the blind guiding the blind.

"So it is difficult as they're two good players who are trying to recover form.

"I think Bayern will be looking at that and thinking, 'We could get this guy we really wanted for maybe pennies on the pound at some point in the future."

2 Woltemade has featured in Juventus' last two Serie A games Credit: Getty



Woltemade still waiting to get off the mark for Juve

Woltemade's two appearances for Juventus so far have been as a substitute, and he's played just 44 minutes in total.

He's only managed to muster three shots in that time, all of them off target.

His loan departure came after he had made two appearances for Newcastle early in the season.

He played the entirety of the Carabao Cup second round win over West Brom before coming off the bench to set up Yoane Wissa's goal in the 2-0 Premier League victory at Tottenham.



Nonetheless, he was loaned out to Juve on deadline day.

He'll hope to get off the mark for the Bianconeri when they host Dutch side NEC Nijmegen in their Europa League opener on Thursday.

Sports.title: ‘A total mess’ – LaLiga club due to move into 70,000 World Cup stadium could be relegated after sacking manager
Sports.content:
‘A total mess’ – LaLiga club due to move into 70,000 World Cup stadium could be relegated after sacking manager

Valencia are in disarray and must avoid LaLiga relegation ahead of the move to their new stadium.

That's according to European football journalists Kevin Hatchard and Andy Brassell as they sit winless at the bottom of Spain's top flight.



3 Valencia are at risk of being relegated with their dismal start to the season Credit: Getty

After their 1-0 defeat to Sevilla on Friday night, Valencia have just one point to show for their efforts with five matches played in LaLiga.

Carlos Corberan, formerly in charge of Championship side West Brom, has been sacked as head coach of his boyhood club amid their poor run.

Ex-Chelsea chief Ron Gourlay has also been dismissed from his role as CEO of Football at Valencia, who were crowned Spanish champions in the 2003/04 season.



They are now on a treacherous path towards what would be a shock relegation just months before moving into their new stadium.

Valencia will leave their iconic Mestalla for the 70,000-capacity Nou Mestalla, which is set to cost £275million at completion and one of Spain's proposed venues for the 2030 World Cup.



However, Ches Blanquinegros have been warned that they cannot afford to be relegated to LaLiga 2 before their relocation.

Valencia were 'unforgivably terrible' at Sevilla

On Trans Europe Express, Hatchard said: "We started this with Mestalla, and the reason is it's a total mess at the Mestalla...



"Corberan, for a Valencia coach, has lasted a while, actually. He saved them from the drop in his first season, they improved upon that last season. But the truth is, this goes way beyond coaching...

"You invest nothing, what do you expect?" Brassell interjected, before Hatchard added: "This is about Peter Lim (owner), really, this is about the ownership, as it has been for a long, long time."

Brassell agreed and explained: "When you look at the fact that they're due to move into their new Mestalla, their new stadium that's been 20 years in the making, at the start of next season, they really need to be in the top flight for that.

3 Corberan was dismissed having been appointed in December 2024 Credit: Getty



"We're talking about a 70,000 stadium that's obviously going to have a part in the next World Cup. It's been through various different incarnations, abandonments, restructures.

"For ages, the facade and the foundations were just sitting there for people to look at, it was like a monument of folly, really. Whereas, now they're really close to doing it, they have to have a team that's worthwhile playing in it. 70,000 seats to fill is a lot.

"You go back to last week when they were playing against Barcelona... talking of Rodri, he's had a week where he's very much had his tail between his legs, because he got caught on TV saying to a couple of his Barcelona teammates, 'These lot are absolute rubbish'.

"Which is fine, obviously people say that sort of stuff to their teammates. Normally in the dressing room, or normally at the training ground, not in a stadium that's got 36 cameras in it and loads of other people taking social videos, and all the rest of it.



"Lip reading is the second Spanish national sport after watching football, it's very much a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday sort of thing, so he basically had to apologise for it.

"One of the last things that Corberan did as Valencia coach was say, 'I don't accept your apology', basically. Of course, he should have been apologising himself for the performance that they gave at Sevilla on Friday night.

3 Valencia's new stadium could welcome a second-tier team next season Credit: Getty

"Sevilla are in an even bigger financial hole than Valencia - they made Sevilla look like France '98, they were absolutely, unforgivably terrible.



"I feel sorry for Corberan, but the last couple of performances have been dreadful. Even with the disquiet at the club and, as you say, it's nothing new, the performances have got to be better than that.

"I don't think they've got one of the worst three squads in the division, but Lim is going to have to put his hand in his pocket at some point."

Valencia drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo in their season opener before 1-0 and 3-1 defeats to Real Betis and Deportivo de A Coruna respectively.

A 5-0 thumping by Barcelona preceded the loss away at Sevilla, with Alaves and Real Sociedad up next before the international break.

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher has never been prouder than about what sons did to angry Man United fans
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher has never been prouder than about what sons did to angry Man United fans

Noel Gallagher says his heart swelled with pride as his son 'got stuck into' Manchester United fans at Sunday's derby.

Oasis star and die-hard Manchester City fan Gallagher was in the away end at Old Trafford as Erling Haaland's controversial goal won the game for the ten-man visitors.



3 Gallagher got to celebrate a Man City win on a rare trip to Old Trafford Credit: Getty

'My heart is full of pride'

And Gallagher revealed his son Sonny got thoroughly swept up in the occasion.

Speaking to Andy Goldstein and former Man United goalkeeper Ben Foster on talkSPORT DriveTime, he said: "There comes a point in your time as a father where you look at your children and you think, 'My god, I brought you up well' – when they feel it as much as you do and when they get it.

"Let's not forget, when you're in that away end and the United fans are in front of you, they're giving it to you as much as you're giving it to them.



"But he made the newspapers today and my heart is full of pride for my sons who got stuck into it yesterday and got stuck into the United fans as well."

A special day for the Gallagher family

Gallagher also revealed that it was his sons' – Sonny and brother Donovan – first trip to an away Manchester derby.



The pair were spotted jokingly taunting United fans by making crude gestures from the stands.

"Ordinarily I wouldn't [go]," Gallagher continued. "I don't like going to Old Trafford because it can get a bit spicy getting in and out, but they were there.



"They were so keen to go because they'd never been, so I went for them really and they got stuck into it big time and it was a great, great day."

Understandably, Gallagher was thrilled about the manner of City's victory.

Enzo Maresca's side played more than hour with ten men after Phil Foden's contentious red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

3 Haaland won the game with his sixth goal of the season Credit: Getty



3

"Obviously we celebrated like made for about five seconds [after Haaland's goal which was initially disallowed for offside]," Gallagher said. "We thought he looked offside even this morning.

"I was watching Match of the Day. He looks offside on the telly, so everyone thought it was offside, but it's the toenail of a boot.

"And no one's talking about the finish. How he got it in and across the other side of the goal is unbelievable.



"The fact that has gone our way [and] our whole strategy with 10 men is unbelievable."

Oasis to hit the road again in 2027

Gallagher also discussed Oasis' latest tour announcement, following their momentous 2025 reunion.

The Britpop icons will play 38 dates across Europe and North America next year.

They include a whopping 11 nights at City's Etihad Stadium and a return to Knebworth, the site of their legendary 1996 shows.

Sports.title: Why is the upcoming international break three weeks long? England to play four games in first games since World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
Why is the upcoming international break three weeks long? England to play four games in first games since World Cup heartbreak

England return to action this month for the first time since the World Cup in a new-look September international break.

Previously, there were four breaks of two-week windows during the Premier League season – in September, October, November and March, followed by a June international window.



4 England were left heartbroken at the World Cup as 60 years of hurt continued Credit: Getty

This format saw each country play two matches per window, but that is all set to change this year.

Instead of separate breaks in September and October, there will now be a three-week gap for international fixtures across late September and early October, with the two windows merging.

Countries will play four matches across two weeks as opposed to the traditional two matches in a week format.



The shake-up leaves England with a jam-packed schedule, as they return two months after their wait for major silverware continued with a heart-breaking World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Thomas Tuchel's side face some stern tests, as they prepare to face world champions Spain, Croatia and Czechia twice in the Nations League.



There is certain to be plenty of eyes on these games, with fans keen to see how Tuchel responds in the wake of huge criticism over the circumstances of his side's World Cup exit.

Why will the September international break last three weeks?

A number of reasons are behind the decision to merge the September and October international breaks this season.



This is partly due to the date of the World Cup final, with Spain emerging victorious over Argentina on July 19.

The New York showdown's timing made it the latest date for a summer World Cup since 1966.

Player welfare and travel considerations were taken into account when the changes were made.

4 Thomas Tuchel has one less international break to prepare for this Autumn Credit: Getty



By reducing the number of international breaks, this means some players will have to travel less from one continent to another for their international fixtures.

This could hugely benefit African or South American players who play their domestic football in Europe and usually have to travel cross-continent on several occasions to represent their national teams.

While the five-break schedule was previously the norm, there were some exceptions to this, such as when there was a major tournament like the World Cup, Africa Cup of Nations or European Championship.

The move to switch to an extended September break was approved by the FIFA Council in March 2023.



Meanwhile, the removal of the October break also ensures there will be an extra week of domestic football in the calendar.

When are England playing?

England will play their first match since the World Cup when they take on Spain at Wembley on Saturday, September 26.

4 England ultimately collected a bronze medal at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

They then face Czechia away three days later on Tuesday, September 29.



In another quick turnaround, the Three Lions as they travel to Croatia on Saturday, October 3.

They then wrap up the international break by hosting Czechia at Wembley in the return Nations League clash on Tuesday, October 6.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of all four matches, and talkSPORT.com will be right across all of the action too.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

4 Wembley will be hosting two Nations League games in the upcoming September international break Credit: Getty



What happens after the March international break?

Once England have completed the two-week international break, the players will return to their clubs until early November.

They will then have a traditional week-long international window between November 9 and November 17.

2026-27 International Windows September 21 to October 6 - Four matches

November 9 to 17 - Two matches

March 22 to 30 - Two matches

June 7 to 15 - Two matches

A four-month break from England action will follow, with the national team returning to action for a week in March 2027.

The last international break of the 2026/27 campaign falls in June next year, running from Monday, June 7 to Tuesday, 15 June.

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher says Liam Gallagher will be sober for Oasis tour and reveals moment they decided to do 2027 gigs
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher says Liam Gallagher will be sober for Oasis tour and reveals moment they decided to do 2027 gigs

Noel Gallagher has revealed that his brother Liam will be 'off the booze' for Oasis' newly announced 2027 tour.

The legendary Britpop band have confirmed 38 more dates for 2027, including a return to Knebworth – where they famously played two nights in 1996 at the height of their fame – and 11 nights at the Etihad Stadium, home to Manchester City, who the Gallagher brothers famously support.

3 Oasis returned to the stage last year after 16 years of fans wondering whether they ever would again Credit: Getty

And Gallagher exclusively told talkSPORT when they made the decision to carry on playing, having ended their 16-year hiatus in 2025.

That tour included five gigs at Wembley, and it was there that it became clear that it wouldn't be the end of their comeback.

When Oasis decided they were 'going to do it'

Joining Andy Goldstein and former Manchester United goalkeeper Ben Foster on talkSPORT DriveTime, Gallagher confirmed: "It was after the second Wembley show [we decided to tour again].

"Nobody really knew what was going to happen, how it was going to go.

"We did Cardiff and Manchester and by the time we got to Wembley…. it was decided we were going to do it."

Gallagher, who hinted on talkSPORT earlier this month that a tour announcement was imminent, also explained that Oasis planned all along to play on the continent.



"We couldn't not do Europe because our fans in Italy and France and Germany and Spain have been brilliant," he added. "It was always the plan to do that.

Oasis will also cross the pond to to perform in Las Vegas and Boston.



"The Vegas and Boston gigs we were supposed to do last year," Gallagher said.

Early nights for the Gallagher brothers

And while the band will be on the road for a good two months, Gallagher admits they can't 'do it like they did in the 90s'.

"Liam will be off the booze and I wasn't for the last tour, but I might be for this.

"You've just got to go to bed early. We can't do it like we did in the 90s; we can't even do it like we did in the 2000s, but you've got to pick your battles."

3 Both Gallagher brothers could do away with drinking on next year's tour Credit: Getty

Asked what he thought was the best show of the 2025 tour, Gallagher gave a someone surprising answer.

"The second night at the River Plate stadium [El Monumental] is one of the gigs that none of us will ever get," he replied. "You had to be there.

"People don't want to hear it after the World Cup, but those people in that country [Argentina], that stadium, they're sent from heaven. It's unbelievable when Oasis play in Buenos Aries."

Gallagher was also asked about the prospect of releasing new music.

Oasis' seventh and most recent album, 'Dig Out Your Soul' was released back in 2008.

But fans will have to wait for fresh material for the time being at least, with Gallagher shooting down any suggestion of a return to the studio: "There won't be any new music."
