Sports.title: Former Premier League striker goes viral for calling out Howard Webb live on air and hitting out at 'unacceptable' decisions - as ex-ref Dermot Gallagher defends officials after Manchester derby blunder
Sports.content:
Jay Bothroyd has made waves on social media for calling out Pro Ref chief Howard Webb live on Sky Sports.

Webb and his referees have come under fire yet again following their Manchester derby slip up, which saw Erling Haaland's winning goal allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez clearly being offside in the build-up.

VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from duty for this weekend as a result of the fallout.

And Bothroyd, who played for the likes of Cardiff and Wolves in his career, has been one of the people leading the backlash as he let loose on Sky.

Bothroyd clashed with former top-level referee Dermot Gallagher, who had claimed referees 'know the law inside out'.

'Why did they get it wrong then?' the former forward asked.

Jay Bothroyd (right) has gone viral after calling out Howard Webb following the Manchester derby officiating blunder

When he was told the officials likely 'lost focus', a frustrated Bothroyd replied: 'This is the thing. To me, that is unacceptable. You can't lose focus. That is their job. Their only job is to look at this - they are under no pressure, they are in a room.

'There is more than one (VAR official). They need to be getting that right, it's as simple as that. And to be saying sorry afterwards, that's not good enough. Let's be real here - Michael Carrick is under pressure now. He could lose his job because of them making a bad decision and saying sorry. "Sorry, Michael, we've made a bad decision, but you've been sacked".'

Sky then showed a clip of Pro Ref chief Howard Webb saying a similar goal that United scored in the derby three years ago 'shouldn't happen again'.

Bothroyd continued: 'First of all, I need to say this, put the camera on me. Howard Webb, come on this show when it's live and speak to us, because you need to explain to us, so I can put you in the spotlight and ask you questions.

'You need to come and speak to me live on this show about this incident. Because I need to know this. We keep on hearing all these things, and I don't understand them.

'There are laws there, and they are not being followed. The understanding. The interpretation. Even yesterday (in the derby), they are saying sorry then trying to explain it and they are digging themselves a bigger hole.

'I don't understand it. I will put my money on it now and say it - this is the easiest decision I'm going to see all year and it's four games in.'

Despite Gallagher's protests, Bothroyd received widespread support for his words.

Erling Haaland's goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez standing offside

Fernandez moved to head the ball, clearly impacting United's Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens

One fan wrote on X: 'Jay Bothroyd calling out Howard Webb on live TV was cinema. GOATed behaviour.'

Another posted: 'I watched this live. Jay Bothroyd has never backed down and always real. I love the way he quizzes referee Dermot Gallagher on Ref Watch. He's one of my favourites. Top player. Top analyst. Top man.'

A third shared: 'Standing ovation for Jay Bothroyd. Proper one.'

Webb regularly appears on pre-recorded TNT Sports show 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up', in which he analyses refereeing calls from games.

It was pointed out to Bothroyd that Webb has previously spoken live on incidents, but the forward called for him to go on Sky Sports too.

United defender Lisandro Martinez led the protests from United players after the game.

He said on Sky: 'It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice.

'I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He (Fernandez) was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that's why Haaland was free at the back.

'It's so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they're coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half. They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It's unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Leeds sniffed vulnerability and went for the kill in 4-1 horror show for Newcastle, writes CRAIG HOPE - this was a warning over where their season could end up, while Whites eye race for Europe
Sports.content:
Identical records coming into this, poles and goals apart coming out. Leeds bullied and bettered Newcastle and are deservedly up to third in the Premier League. Their unbeaten start is genuine and so are the prospects of them challenging for European football this season, nearly a quarter of a century after their last continental campaign. Newcastle’s start always felt less real, and so it proved on a night when Daniel Farke’s side were as brilliant and boisterous as those in the stands. Elland Road was a bear pit and, from the off, it was clear that their visitors were in for a mauling. To think, they’re in the process of making this place even bigger and more intimidating. Those words capture Dominic Calvert-Lewin, too. He should be in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad this week after a centre-forward showing that was as powerful as it was precise. He deserved two goals - the dubious awards panel gave his first to a strand of Jayden Bogle’s hair - but there is no such committee to rob him of the man-of-the-match prize. ‘It was a top-class performance during the whole game,’ said Farke. ‘But we can’t get cocky or too big-time. This should give us huge confidence going forward. ‘As for Dominic, he is one of the best strikers in the league in this form.’ This 3-0 Leeds defeat marked the night the result caught up with their performances Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star of the show as he continued his fine form at Elland Road For Newcastle, this was a night when the result finally caught up with performance. Unbeaten in three at the outset of the Premier League and lauded for their summer business, autumn and winter might not be so cheery on the evidence of this horror show. Matthias Jaissle’s side were three down by half-time, and it was no surprise at all. Be that on the basis of what played out here or, more so, performances of the past 10 days. An unconvincing 1-0 win at Millwall in the Carabao Cup came on the back of an equally sketchy 2-2 draw at home to Bournemouth. This, then, was in the post, and Calvert-Lewin was the home side’s delivery man. He was not the only one to profit from opposition weak in the tackle, wayward in the pass and woefully short of ideas in attack. Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu bossed a midfield that was superior by every metric. At times, you wondered if the hosts had an extra man. You wondered more how Newcastle have won such praise for their character and resilience in recent weeks. There were none of those traits on show this time. Jaissle said: ‘Not only one thing went wrong. We couldn’t bring the fundamentals in the first half. We couldn’t match the intensity of Leeds, in duals or physicality. That should be the basics of football. Unforced errors were taking place. We needed to find the right reaction on the pitch, and we struggled with that.’ Newcastle’s numbers have not felt sustainable. They had conceded a league-high 45 shots over the first three games and, at the other end, their cumulative XG was just over one per 90 minutes. This will infuriate traditionalists - those who cherish the scoreline - but an expected league position had Newcastle 19th going into this weekend. A lot, it seemed, rested on the slender shoulders on Matias Fernandez-Pardo in reversing the numbers. The 21-year-old, a £51million marquee arrival from Lille this month, was making his full debut. ‘Eden Hazard without the end product’ was how one Belgian journalist described the forward on the day he signed, much to the irritation of black-and-white ears listening on local radio. So, was there any merit in the unflattering assessment? MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 6; Bogle 7, Ampadu 8, Tanaka 8 (Aaronson 72, 6), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 72, 6); Stach 6, Okafor 7 (Wilson 72, 6); Calvert-Lewin 9 Subs: Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha Manager: Daniel Farke 8 Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 57), Thiaw 5, Botman 3, Hall 5; Miley 4 (Bamba 80), Gonzalez 5 (Steur 19, 4); Murphy 4 (Toure 57, 6), Wissa 5, Barnes 4; Fernandez-Pardo 4 (Willock 57, 4) Subs: Pope, Livramento, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley Manager: Matthias Jaissle 4 Ref: M Salisbury 7 After 25 minutes, the hot-takes felt cold, given Fernandez-Pardo had touched the ball only four times, and one of those was an accidental handball inside his own area. By the time he made way in the 57th minute, the touch count had reached 15, but none of them memorable. What Fernandez-Pardo learnt here is that speed of foot counts for nothing when faced with speed of thought. ‘We had to bury the game after a good start and that is what we did,’ said Farke. Leeds’ third goal on the stroke of half-time was the one that sealed the zip on Newcastle’s body bag. That goal was about Calvert-Lewin’s force and Newcastle’s complete lack of it, the striker barging his way through Sven Botman before finishing from six yards. The opener, 13 minutes earlier, was officially a Lewis Miley own goal, but it owed everything to Ao Tanaka, who started the move amid space in midfield and finished it amid space in midfield. It was his 20-yard shot that deflected in off the Newcastle youngster, who like many of his team-mates endured a torrid night. His midfield sidekick, Sean Steur, was guilty of the stray pass that set Leeds on their way to a second, when Calvert-Lewin headed in from a James Justin cross, only for replays to reveal the ball clipping the head of Bogle. Marquee signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo struggled, but that says more about the failings behind him Technical weaknesses were always likely to catch up with the Magpies this season The fourth, in the 59th minute, was a smart Noah Okafor finish after he reacted quickest to a loose ball from a long throw-in. But Leeds had been quicker to first, second and third balls all night. The home fans were chanting for five when Baz Toure nicked an 89th-minute consolation. The away end had long since lost their voice and their solemn mood reflected a team who had made precious little noise on the pitch. This was a brutal reality check and serves as a warning for where their season could be headed. Leeds, meanwhile, are looking up - at Arsenal and Manchester City.

Sports.title: Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post
Sports.content:
Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eye injuries.

The Englishman last fought in October last year, when his title defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no-contest after multiple eye pokes.

Aspinall was subsequently diagnosed with a rare condition called Brown's syndrome in both eyes and has had multiple surgeries, but he is still not ready to compete.

He wrote on Instagram: 'I’m absolutely gutted. I’ve chased this dream since I was 10 years old.

'I’m not done. Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream. I’ll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible.

'What makes this particularly difficult is that many of the complications I’m dealing with are a result of fouls that changed the course of my career. Fighters rely on officials to enforce the rules and protect us in those moments, and it’s hard to still be dealing with the consequences today.'

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eyes injuries

He was diagnosed with a rare condition Brown's syndrome following an eye poke at UFC 321

He also said: 'Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now.

'I’ve had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

'I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye. This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear.'

He added: 'I’ve now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I’ve asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don’t want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it’s like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title.'

Aspinall returned to training in June with a view to fighting Gane in September but the wait will have to go on.

In August, Aspinall rebuffed suggestions that he would leave the UFC.

Against Gane in October, Aspinall retained his UFC heavyweight title via no contest in an anticlimactic ending to the main event at UFC 321 that saw the Brit struggling to see and rushed to hospital.

He does intend to return to fighting in the UFC but is unable to at the moment

After four minutes of the first round of the fight in Abu Dhabi, as Aspinall attempted a kick, Gane went at his rival with a punch and inadvertently raked his fingers across his eyes. A five-minute timeout ensued, and the doctor stepped in.

Aspinall was spotted telling the doctor: 'I can't see,' with the doctor himself telling the referee that he had 'no immediate concerns about the globe'.

After four minutes of the five allocated, however, the fight was waved off as a no-contest.

'All that training for that,' Aspinall said. 'What the f*** is he doing?

'He got warned twice before it. Twice before it he got warned for it and he f***ing did it again.'

Gane, however, said: 'I didn't do it on purpose. I know what it's like to have an eye poke, because when I fought Derrick Lewis, I got an eye poke and I was seeing two of Derrick Lewis for a full round.

'During a bit of the round and the rest of the round, I saw two of Derrick Lewis. So I'm not going to say, he's a liar.'

Aspinall, who was sat with his eye strapped up, added: 'I could feel how deep it was in my eye. It feels like the back of my eyeball is hurting. It feels like someone's touched the back of my eyeball.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment 'raging' Dominic Calvert-Lewin is told by referee his goal was taken off him after team-mate's tiny deflection
Sports.content:
Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave a hilarious reaction to being told his side's second goal had been taken away from him on Monday night. The Whites thumped Newcastle 4-1 in a stellar performance at Elland Road, with four different players, ultimately, on the scoresheet for the home side. Calvert-Lewin scored the third goal, but thought he had also netted the second when he headed in from James Justin's cross. But replays showed his header came off team-mate Jayden Bogle, and the full back was officially credited with the goal. Sky cameras managed to capture the exact moment Calvert-Lewin was told the goal wasn't actually his, with his face dropping in disbelief when he was told by an official at half-time. 'The ref told me at half-time they gave it to Jayden,' he said on Sky Sports after the match. 'I didn't even know he was there as I got up early and bang. I'll take the assist.' This is the hilarious moment Dominic Calvert-Lewin (right) found out Leeds' second goal against Newcastle had actually been awarded to Jayden Bogle (left) Calvert-Lewin joked after the game that he would be looking to appeal the decision Bogle, meanwhile, said: 'I didn't know anything about it. I said to the ref I didn't fancy telling him at half-time. Even during the game he was still a bit raging. He's happy with the points though.' And the saga carried on after the game. Calvert-Lewin and Bogle posed for a snap together, with the forward writing: 'He's told me that it didn't touch him. How do I appeal this scandalous decision?' He also tagged the Premier League. Calvert-Lewin would later finish well from Tarik Muharemovic's pass, making it 3-0 to his side. Lewis Miley's own goal opened the scoring and Noah Okafor's finish made it 4-0 before Bazoumana Traore netted a late consolation. The result moved Leeds up to third in the Premier League, with Newcastle sat in 12th.

Sports.title: West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer
Sports.content:
West Ham paid tribute to their cult hero and 'gentle giant' Ludek Miklosko who has died at the age of 64.

Miklosko kept 126 clean sheets in eight years with the Hammers and is perhaps best remembered for an inspirational series of saves to deny Manchester United the title in 1995.

The popular Czech, signed from Banik Ostrava for £300,000, later returned to the club as goalkeeper coach and fans have continued to sing his name for many years.

West Ham's players held a moment of silence before training on Monday, and the club will honour him before Wednesday's Carabao Cup third round tie against Fulham.

There are also plans for a tribute at next month's Championship fixture against Queens Park Rangers, where Miklosko spent the final three years of his playing career.

'Rest in peace Ludek, our beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man,' said West Ham in a statement released on Monday.

Legendary former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 after a cancer battle

The much-loved Czech 'gentle giant' made 373 outings for West Ham and also played for QPR

'Ludo', left, was a hugely popular figure at West Ham and tributes have been pouring in for him

Miklosko, who won 42 international caps and represent Czechoslovakia at the World Cup in 1990, was diagnosed with cancer in 2021 and announced three years later his decision to withdraw from further treatment.

His son Martin said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of my Dad Ludek, following a brave and courageous battle with cancer.

'On behalf of my Mum and my family, I would like to sincerely thank the fans and everyone at West Ham United Football Club for the kind wishes, thoughts and prayers that were sent to my Dad during his illness.

'We know that the many messages and wishes from his former team-mates and fans alike were a huge sense of comfort to him in his battle with cancer and gave him the strength to not give up and keep fighting for as long as he could.

'We are heartbroken at his loss but take huge comfort from the immense support he received from all of you, along with the knowledge that he is now at peace and no longer suffering.

'Dad simply loved West Ham United, and especially hearing his name sung loud and proud at every game. The club, and its fans, were and always will be a part of our family, so thank you all from the bottom of our hearts.'

Sports.title: Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tottenham forward Richarlison has taken aim at his manager Roberto De Zerbi after the Spurs boss rejected the chance to call him up for his side's Carabao Cup game at Liverpool.

The forward has been left out of his club's Premier League squad, but is available for selection in the League Cup.

Spurs have failed to score in their first four Premier League games this season, an embarrassment heightened by the omission of Richarlison – last season's top scorer with 12 goals – from the squad.

'Nothing changes in my project, in my idea,' said De Zerbi. 'I am sorry for the goals we didn't score, but we have the qualities to score goals.

'We are building a new project, a new team. I can't change my opinion about the players if they don't win or don't score. They are very good players.

'If we want to change from the last two seasons, we have to be stronger and believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. You can change players or change coaches, change, change, change, and nothing changes. Or you stay humble, with the right spirit to work.

Richarlison has taken aim at Roberto De Zerbi after his manager revealed he will not play the Brazilian in the League Cup

'I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.'

But Richarlison has snapped back. Taking to Instagram, he replied to an X post around De Zerbi's comments with a crying emoji, and then shared a screenshot of the post to Instagram with the caption: 'Why' with another crying emoji.

Richarlison started the league opener at Brentford, but was told he can leave before a move to Everton collapsed and links to Trabzonspor failed to turn into a move.

After he did not agree personal terms with boyhood club Vasco on Friday, he was in attendance for Spurs' goalless draw with Everton, but will remain on the sidelines.

De Zerbi, who will be without Sandro Tonali against Liverpool after the midfielder picked up a knock, took his players out to dinner last week as he did in April, after they lost at Sunderland in his first game in charge. They returned to Mediterranean restaurant Bacchanalia in Mayfair and the Spurs boss picked up the bill.

'Something to eat, some water, some beers,' said De Zerbi. 'It is a pleasure.'

De Zerbi pored over the first half-hour of Saturday's 0-0 draw with Everton to analyse why his side could not convert their dominance into goals.

'We played 25-30 minutes very well,' said De Zerbi. 'We could have scored two. We maybe lost confidence because we didn't score. We have to improve.'

Richarlison, having demanded to leave Spurs in the summer and then failed to agree personal terms with Everton, Trabzonspor or Vasco da Gama, will remain out in the cold.

'We lost at Brentford 3-0 [on the opening day] with Richarlison,' De Zerbi added. 'Maybe you forgot. Just to remind you.'

Sports.title: John McEnroe's 'unprofessional' and 'belittling' comments are slammed as the 'final straw' by angry US Open fans
Sports.content:
John McEnroe's 'unprofessional' and 'belittling' comments are slammed as the 'final straw' by angry US Open fans

ESPN is facing calls to axe John McEnroe after he controversially pleaded for Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz to return to their best in wake of Alexander Zverev's US Open win.

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over home favorite Ben Shelton on Sunday.

The No 1 seed, whose service routine has sparked calls for a rule change, broke the hearts of a New York crowd who hoped Shelton would become the first American man to win a major since 2003.

But he was beaten 6-3 7-6 5-7 6-2 by Zverev and afterwards a clip went viral from ESPN's coverage of the US Open final.

'So the drought continues but the rebirth of Sascha Zverev also continues into 2027 - Down Under awaits, huh?' lead announcer Chris Fowler said, looking ahead to the Australian Open.

'Get healthy Carlos and Jannik!' responded McEnroe, the seven-time Grand Slam singles champion who serves as an analyst alongside his brother Patrick.

This is how the commentary feed ended after the Zverev and Shelton US Open trophy ceremony.



"Get healthy Carlos and Jannik."



"Please"



😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/sUbWxJXQAa — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) September 13, 2026

John McEnroe is facing a backlash over his comments after Alexander Zverev's US Open win

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over Ben Shelton

Both Alcaraz and Sinner have battled injury issues over recent months, with world No 1 Sinner missing the US Open with a knee problem, while Alcaraz returned at Flushing Meadows after more than four months out with wrist damage.

But McEnroe's comments sparked fury among some fans, who accused the tennis legend of being 'unprofessional' and 'belittling the sport.'

'Sorry, this should be the final straw for John McEnroe,' one supporter wrote. 'Unprofessional, belittling the sport and stealing the spotlight from the champion and runner up seconds after victory.'

Another added: 'McEnroe has to go. Carlos is healthy and he played, It's not Zverev's fault that Jannik's knee doesn't work. It's his moment and he won fair and square… this is honestly pathetic.'

Others defended the 67-year-old, however, insisting his comments were part of a discussion looking forward to the 2027 season. 'It’s exactly what most tennis fans are thinking,' one said.

It is not the first time that McEnroe has faced a backlash over comments he made at this US Open. He was earlier accused of being 'disrespectful' in the wake of Novak Djokovic's first-round exit.

After Djokovic was beaten by world No 49 Mariano Navone, McEnroe joked that the Argentine would be 'playing [his] second round on Court 21.'

Sports.title: Expert lip reader reveals what Roberto De Zerbi angrily told Mathys Tel after Tottenham's drab 0-0 draw against Everton - as goal drought rumbles on after £320m spend
Sports.content:
Expert lip reader reveals what Roberto De Zerbi angrily told Mathys Tel after Tottenham's drab 0-0 draw against Everton - as goal drought rumbles on after £320m spend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

An expert lip reader has shed light on what went on between Roberto De Zerbi and Mathys Tel during their heated conversation after Tottenham's draw with Everton.

Spurs remain winless after four games and are yet to score a goal following another drab display on Saturday against David Moyes' side.

After the match, De Zerbi approached Tel on the pitch and appeared to give him a dressing down, with the forward having struggled to make an impact after coming off the bench as a makeshift striker.

Fans have since speculated about the tense interaction, with some suggesting it hinted at signs of a falling out between the pair.

One even appeared to claim that Tel had bitten back at De Zerbi by saying: 'I was here to play football.'

However, Nicola Hickling, expert lip reader and founder of LipReader, has revealed what was actually said.

An expert lip reader has shed light on what went on between Roberto De Zerbi and Mathys Tel

The pair were involved in a heated conversation after Tottenham's 0-0 draw against Everton

Hickling claims De Zerbi said to Tel: 'You're playing like a stud,' suggesting that the forward was running around aimlessly like a horse.

In the clip, the Spurs boss can then be seen to spin, as if he was playing as a striker, with Hickling adding that he said: 'Like that. I need like that, attack focus.'

Tel is said to have replied: 'Yeah, but then I went back to play for the ball.'

Speaking after the game, De Zerbi offered further context on what had gone on, with his second comment seemingly suggesting that Tel needs to stop playing with his back to goal.

'Yes, I coached him on the pitch,' De Zerbi said in his press conference. 'The body shape of a striker. The striker can play with the shoulder on the goal.

'If we are playing with (James) Maddison, (Mohammed) Kudus and Savio, he has to play as a striker, and the striker has to look at the goal, no?

'Or on the cross of Robertson. He has to stay inside because he started (his career) as a striker. Now he's playing as a winger, but he started in his career as a striker.'

Tel was dropped to the bench for the Everton clash after De Zerbi publicly criticised his display against Nottingham Forest the week before, yet the Spurs boss insisted there were no issues between the pair of them.

He added: 'But I love Mathys as a player, as a guy. There is not a problem.'

Tottenham are back in action on Tuesday when they travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup third round, before they entertain Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss

Jamie Carragher says he was "really disappointed" with the actions of Bruno Fernandes during the incident which led to Phil Foden's red card in the loss against Manchester City

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was not impressed with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Sky Sports)

Jamie Carragher has condemned the behaviour of Bruno Fernandes following the incident that led to Phil Foden being sent off in the Manchester derby.

‌



The Manchester City midfielder was shown a straight red card after aiming a kick at the midriff of Fernandes, who had left Foden on the ground following a coming together by the touchline. The Manchester United captain then sent his foot into the small of Foden's back, sparking the violent reaction which curtailed his involvement in the game.

‌



Erling Haaland went on to win the game for City following a highly dubious VAR intervention which, along with Foden's red card, became one of the major talking points from the derby.

‌



Fernandes escaped punishment for his part in the clash with Foden and Carragher has now questioned the Portugal international for the manner of his reaction after the 'kick'.

Sports.title: Four Man Utd players destroyed after painful Man City loss - 'They're walking'
Sports.content:
Four Man Utd players destroyed after painful Man City loss - 'They're walking'

Manchester United were beaten 1-0 by Man City in the Premier League on Sunday, with the Red Devils failing to take advantage of their opponents playing with 10 men for 67 minutes

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo were among the Manchester United players criticised by Jaap Stam (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Jaap Stam has criticised Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha following Sunday's derby defeat to Manchester City. The Red Devils suffered a 1-0 loss at home to their fierce rivals despite facing 10 men for 67 minutes plus added time.

‌



United boss Michael Carrick has now presided over the club's joint-worst opening to a Premier League season, matching last term's poor beginning under Ruben Amorim and the 1992-93 campaign. Carrick took over from the dismissed Portuguese manager on a temporary basis in January and delivered an impressive recovery that secured a third-place finish.

‌



However, United's sluggish opening has placed the former midfielder under increased pressure after being given the role permanently in May. Carrick's side languish in 13th position after four matches, a sequence that has featured defeat at Hull City and a frustrating stalemate at Everton.

‌



Now, former United centre-half Stam has delivered a scatching verdict on United and their players. He told Viaplay: "If you look at City and if you look at this game, it was easy for them today, even with 10 men.

"I was asking myself as well: the United team coming off the pitch, what are they thinking? Would they be thinking they've done everything that they can Is that it?

"Even in playing it out from the back, it was easy, one-two, keep the ball a little bit longer at your feet, somebody else is taking up different positions. You play it, make a little one-two, you're out and they can go and attack.

"Against 10 men, even if it's City with the quality that they have, you would expect United to be on the front foot every time, to be very, very aggressive, even the strikers tracking back. Then, of course, and that's a very important thing as well.

‌



"If you have possession and they are dropping a little bit deeper, use the side, use the width of the game a little bit, put crosses in the box. But now sometimes, you feel like when they're playing, there's not a real idea in how to get to opportunities and how to make it difficult for the opposition to score goals."

View 2 Images Jaap Stam has had his say on United's derby defeat (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

City's winner at Old Trafford sparked controversy after Erling Haaland's goal stood despite Enzo Fernandez appearing to interfere with play while in an offside position. The Premier League's refereeing body Pro Ref has since acknowledged an "error of judgment" from the VAR officials.

‌



However, reviewing the build-up to Haaland's second-half strike, Stam highlighted what he saw as a worrying lack of urgency from United's forwards in getting back to support their teammates.

He added: "It's a long ball, they win it, City takes over and look at the front four [of United]. They're just walking, they're just looking at the situation,' the Dutchman added.

"A team that really wants to win, the strikers, it's about all the 11, it's about chasing. Against 10 men, it's about tracking back, it's about winning battles.

Article continues below

"From then on, you keep possession, you go out in transition and then you try to create and score goals."

Sports.title: OLI BELL: "We should be telling the world about horse racing's success stories"
Sports.content:
Saturdays history making win from Saffie Osborne in the Betfred St Leger was as good a day on the racecourse as I can remember.

About 30,000 racegoers, revelling in the sunshine, fully aware of the magnitude of what they had just witnessed.

Doncaster and the team at Arena Racing deserve huge credit for the work they put in to make the 250th St Leger a fitting day for the occasion. They were rewarded for their efforts with the fairytale result.

It’s vital that the sport shouts loudly about days like Saturday. All too often recently we have been talking negatively about the future of the sport, and whilst clearly there are challenges ahead, if we keep repeating a negative message then surely that is the message that will seep out into the wider world.

‌



The sport of horse racing on its day, as Saturday highlighted so perfectly, is unmatched. Therefore, repeating, quite loudly that racing has its detractors, or that there are dark clouds on the horizon is a very damaging narrative to put into the public psyche.

This isn’t me saying we should bury our heads in the sand if there is a bad news story but there are plenty of things out of most people’s control.

Of the 30,000-plus at Doncaster on Saturday I reckon 99.99% of them couldn’t give two hoots if Arc, the Jockey Club, Ascot and the RCA were at loggerheads.

View 2 Images ITV presenter Oli Bell says racing should be shouting loudly about the sport's success stories (Image: ITV)

‌



Thankfully Martin Cruddace told me on ITV's The Opening Show that there are positive conversations being had behind the scenes in that space.

But that’s exactly it isn’t it…. There are very smart people in racing, in high powered roles that we need to trust to do their jobs well and for the best interest of the long term health of the sport.

Rather than publicly peddling a narrative of infighting and issues, we need to spend our energies telling the world that racing, no matter anything going on behind the scenes. is truly magical.

Saturday showed us that. Racing always shows us that.

‌



The point is... whenever something good happens we don’t need to air our dirty laundry. We need to be yelling about the fact that racing, a sport that allows men and women to compete equally, has just witnessed a groundbreaking, historic, inspirational moment.

We need to be ensuring every news station is aware of it. We need to be campaigning to get Saffie short listed for BBC SPOTY. We need to be making sure that everyone, whether they like racing or not is aware of these moments of unbridled joy that only the sport of racing can serve up.

In Saffie and soon-to-be-champion jockey Billy Loughnane the sport of racing has two generational stars that can cross into the mainstream and bring new fans into the sport.

Let’s spend more time telling the world about them and their achievements rather then who is bickering with who.

Sports.title: Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action
Sports.content:
Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action

The video assistant referees at the centre of the Erling Haaland Manchester United vs Man City controversy in the Premier League have been stood down by Pro Ref

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's goal against Manchester United was controversially allowed to stand after a lengthy VAR check (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from officiating duty in the wake of the Manchester derby controversy. Donohue and Antrobus were in the video assistant referee booth for Sunday's 1-0 win for Manchester City over rivals United after Erling Haaland's second-half winner.

‌



Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb and the management team are said to have made the decision, which will see the pair out of action at least until after the international break. It comes after Haaland's effort was given despite the on-field decision initially being offside.

‌



It was claimed at the time that the Norwegian was in an onside position with Patrick Dorgu's outstretched leg playing him on and Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, hadn't interfered with play despite making an attempt to connect with Josko Gvardiol's cross.

‌



Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit READ MORE :

OPINION Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola by Andy Dunn

Lisandro Martinez was caught between the offside Fernandez and Haaland, who was behind him. The Argentine was left incensed by the decision and was forced to hold back during an angry interview with Sky Sports on Sunday.

Michael Carrick was also left exasperated from the incident and admitted he was left 'very worried' by the perception from the officials. Pro Ref, formerly the PGMOL, later apologised for an 'error of judgement'.

‌



A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

‌



"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

View 2 Images Haaland's goal was eventually given after a long VAR check (Image: Getty Images)

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Article continues below

Donohue was the lead video assistant referee for the Manchester derby and has not been appointed a top-flight fixture this weekend, a first this term after being involved in three Premier League matches so far. He will not be on duty for the Carabao Cup third round either which sees European clubs in cup action.

The organisation were forced to U-turn on the suggestion that the former Chelsea man hadn't interfered with play following an Premier League Match Centre tweet on X.

It read: "VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

Sports.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough
Sports.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough

Sir Kevin Sinfield, who has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events, describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate" in Rob Burrow

Kevin Sinfield on his last MND challenge

Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the EuroMillions when the going gets tough in his epic MND charity runs.

‌



The shy superhero has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events. He describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate". The friend is rugby league legend and Sir Kevin's former team mate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024 after living with motor neurone disease (MND) for more than four years.

‌



Dad-of-two Sir Kevin dreams of winning the lottery to fund a cure for the disease - and buy a new car for his dad Ray - in times of need. Asked how he handles the mental battle of running more than 30 miles a day, he said: "I dream of winning the EuroMillions. That is my favourite one.

‌



"It is always the same amount, my dad always gets a new car. Then we cure MND with it."

Rugby legend Kevin Sinfield finally knighted in Birthday Honours for MND fundraising heroics READ MORE :

View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the lottery on his epic runs (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

Sir Kevin Sinfield launches latest MND fundraiser

Speaking at Old Trafford where he launched his last fundraiser at the SuperLeague Dream Team event, he admitted that the training "just gets harder" as you grow older.

‌



His aim is to help as many MND sufferers as possible. Rob Burrow, his former Leeds Rhinos team mate, raised more than £20m for MND research. Sir Kevin has added another £11m.

Sir Kevin told how his latest venture will help research to find a cure, and support those who have been diagnosed with the disease.

"I finished the last block of running on Saturday which was my birthday. The challenge now is to stay fit and healthy and be really smart for the next two weeks," he said.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield carries his best friend Rob Burrow over the finishing line of the Leeds Marathon in 2023 (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

"I have not trained harder; it just gets harder and I am getting older. It would be great to find a cure, we are still a fair stretch from that. The cure is the dream for everyone involved.

"In the short term, we have to help the families diagnosed today and tomorrow. We are letting them down, and that has been the case for decades. We can help them.

‌



"Then there is the awareness because it makes such a difference when people know and understand this condition.

"Over past three and four years, at the stops in the running, we have brought people together, and that shows the love support for the MND families.

"And can share in grief for the families who have lost loved ones. I am a shy bloke; I have love for the team who have been immense through all this."

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield is now an England rugby union coach (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

'We did this for Rob'

Asked about the secret of his success, he said they had been "incredibly lucky" with the timing of their first effort during Covid.

He added: "There were no other charity or sporting events, and people wanted to give their money, it was just incredible. I never forget why we started this - it was to run for Rob, it has always been about doing a bit of running for a mate.

‌



"I did a half marathon on Saturday and then had a recovery, and I went for a meal as most people do for their birthday. Juggling family time and work is tough for everybody preparing for a marathon. It is just the same for me."

He has just returned from South Africa where he said he was "chased by a pack of dogs" while training. He has also been to Argentina, where he was told that he might have to 'barricade himself in the hotel' in Buenos Aires during the England v Argentina World Cup semi final.

He has completed an incredible 500km of training over the past few weeks. The dad, from Oldham, Greater Manchester, has also been in touch with Jai Arrow, the forward for the South Sydney Rabbitohs, who announced his immediate retirement from the National Rugby League (NRL) in May after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) at age 30.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin on his Ultra 7 challenge in 2022 (Image: PA)

'There is a war to be won against MND'

Sir Kevin is Australia next year for the rugby World Cup and 'has an idea' about doing one more charity event abroad. But he wanted to bring the curtain down on his UK exploits, with a tour of the rugby league grounds of the North at the end of this month.

"I needed to release the team, and this is something I could do," he added. "The support for Rob and the Burrow family in Leeds is always great.

‌



"I look forward to going back there thanks to my history with the city. I'm also really looking forward going back to the North West, seeing the people who have supported us.

"I know it will be an incredible week. It sounds strange given the rivalry but I always get a warm welcome in Hull and I love going there.

"All the Superleague clubs have been great, after the final on October 3 is over, and the battle is over, there is a war to be won against MND and I hope they can help with that."

‌



He admits that he still "does not like running" but added: "I makes you a better person, and a bit kinder. I would always encourage people to exercise, getting out there in the open air is so good for you, for your mental health. The good thing is that people are always nice to me now.

"Opposition clubs were always respectful to me after I retired from the game, and we have seen the best of our home nations. The fans always turn up with a big smile which is so important and the nice thing is that people don't just talk bout rugby now, they talk about running and the MND community."

View 5 Images Sir Kevin and Rob Burrow are pictured at an event in May 2023 (Image: PA)

‌



Sir Kevin, who turned 46 on Saturday, will visit all 12 English Betfred Super League grounds from Sept 27 to Oct 3 as he completes seven ultra marathons in seven days.

Now an England rugby union coach, he has already completed six epic endurance challenges for MND research. He will start at Hull Kingston Rovers on September 28 and call in at the grounds of the 11 other English top-flight rugby league clubs along the way.

The "7 in 7: The Grand Finale" venture is set to finish on the pitch at Old Trafford ahead of the Super League Grand Final. As part of his challenge, he will run a mile each day alongside people affected by the neurodegenerative illness.

Article continues below

Each day will be separated into 7 km blocks, which Sinfield has to complete within an hour. His route will take him across the Pennines on day five, and that day he will visit Wigan Warriors and Leigh Leopards.

The last run sets off at St Helens, calls at Warrington Wolves, and then heads to Manchester. You can find out full details of this year’s challenge using this link.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola

The world's best manager left at the end of last season after ten glorious and successful years but Enzo Maresca has got his Manchester City side refreshed and raring to go

View 3 Images Erling Haaland could not stop smiling after Manchester City's win at Old Trafford (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Arne Slot’s version of Liverpool in the early stages of the 2025-26 season is a warning to any Premier League manager. Five Premier League matches, five wins, including a victory in the Merseyside derby.

‌



And Slot already had a title in the bank. So when it comes to reading significance into a small sample of games in August and September, the reservations are obvious.

‌



But watching Manchester City on and off the pitch at Old Trafford, it was hard not to wonder if this is a squad that has been re-energised by the managerial change. That sounds heinous to suggest, obviously.

‌



And don’t forget, Pep Guardiola did bow out by winning two trophies in his final season and his team finished as Premier League runners-up. Hardly a shabby campaign.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But even though Guardiola also counted a Manchester derby win - a less controversial 3-0 verdict at the Etihad - amongst his early successes last season, his side lost two of their opening four Premier League games. Enzo Maresca has won four out of four, complementing those wins with a 2-0 Champions League victory in Porto.

All four Premier League wins have been in different styles but the players have quickly bought into Maresca, it seems. Not just the players.

Everyone is happy if your club has just won a Manchester derby with ten men on opposition turf. That goes without saying.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has had the perfect start as Manchester City manager (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

But the reaction of the backroom staff - of which there were plenty - was as involved and as euphoric as City supporters have probably seen for quite some time. Again, it is understandable when you win by a single goal at Old Trafford, having had a player very harshly dismissed early doors.

But it was still significant. If some players and staff have been refreshed by a change of voice and approach, it would not be the biggest surprise. Guardiola was a very demanding manager. Brilliant but demanding, a perfectionist.

‌



Maresca could well turn out to be similarly demanding, but he is still getting to know the different characters at the club. The jury will be out for some time on Maresca’s chances of making a decent fist of the impossible job of following a decade of Pep’s brilliance. Of course it will. He will be measured in trophies.

But derby wins for City do not come much more treasured than the one he helped produce at Old Trafford. Tactically, he got it spot-on, his deployment of Iliman Ndiaye a mini masterstroke. And it is clear he likes a gritty player. Who doesn’t?

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola delivered hundreds of half-time speeches to his Manchester City players (Image: Prime Video)

‌



Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez were arch-disruptors against United and you can expect Maresca’s City to be perhaps a little more feisty than they were under Guardiola. And you can expect them to rise to the challenge.

Guardiola is and was a genius. But Erling Haaland and the players he has left at the Etihad - and, true, a few have gone - will be out to prove a point.

It might only be subconsciously, but they will be out to prove that City’s success over the past ten years was not just down to one man. And perhaps that is why the celebrations at the end of the derby win were even more euphoric.

Sports.title: Howard Webb has serious questions to answer as Pro Ref's new era begins with huge controversy
Sports.content:
Howard Webb has serious questions to answer as Pro Ref's new era begins with huge controversy

Pro Ref find themselves under huge pressure following a weekend of controversy in the Premier League that has left fans, players and managers alike second-guessing their decisions

View 3 Images Webb has been chief of the PGMOL/Pro Ref since 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

There was the big rebrand. We even got the clear mission statement of a crackdown on grappling at corners and a lighter touch on VAR to bring back on-field decisions.

‌



A new name was also supposed to usher in better standards, better officials and fans could actually enjoy and believe what they were seeing on the pitch. A brave new world for Pro Ref (the band formerly known as the PGMOL) - and it has lasted less than a month.

‌



This weekend was so damaging for Howard Webb, referees and VAR. It’s about trust, key decisions and cutting out big errors.

‌



Webb is such a good guy, such a convincing personality and when he was appointed, I thought it was a really good move. But what is happening? Sadly, with such regular big high profile errors, it is damaging him to such an extent that his position should be questioned.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Let’s be clear: it is being questioned by clubs. I was at Old Trafford on Sunday. I was watching from the press box. And I simply could not for the life of me understand what had happened. How on earth was Erling Haaland’s goal allowed to stand?

The VAR cleared up that Haaland was onside. So, fair play. I thought he was miles offside at first glance. That’s what VAR is there for. And it did it’s job.

But what about Enzo Fernandez? It’s so obvious that he was offside and impacted Lisandro Martinez. What did I miss? Was there a touch? I just couldn’t get my head round it.

‌



And I’m someone who reads up on directives, rules and laws of the game. Everyone in the stadium was left in the dark. Gary Neville on the gantry did not know what was going on.

View 3 Images Howard Webb must now be questioned (Image: Getty Images)

It was such a big error. Referee Michael Oliver must have had an inkling. The VARs did not see it. There was utter confusion.

‌



No wonder Manchester United were fuming. It has decided a game. Manchester City get three points. One clear error could win them the title.

It’s up there with Luis Diaz and an actual technical mistake of his goal being ruled out at Tottenham. Liverpool were incensed and that is still looked at as the benchmark for the biggest VAR howler. That was deemed “significant human error.” Pro Ref have held up their hands on Haaland and issued a statement.

Arsenal were also penalized at Sunderland. That is never a penalty given by John Brooks. Never ever, ever. Ezri Konsa punished for a pull down on Dan Ballard. It was six of one, half a dozen of the other and a referee out of his depth.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Oliver was the official at the centre of the Old Trafford storm (Image: Getty Images)

The previous week, I think the officials guessed on Neco Williams and his goal being disallowed for Nottingham Forest against Tottenham. It was probably the right decision. But how did they get there?

There some good young officials coming through. There really are. There’s some good established ones. Oliver being one. But this damages all of them.

‌



Let’s be clear. You cannot stop every error. But you have to be stopping the Old Trafford one. That’s a shocker.

Webb communicates well with clubs. He’s so much better than Mike Riley and those who went before him. But is this working? No.

The game is being undermined by some bad errors, referees and a lack of trust from the fans, the players and managers. The so-called best league in the world cannot stand for this. It is simply not good enough.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
